Sen. Bernie Moreno, a Republican from Ohio, broke his silence around the horrific abuse claims his daughter has leveled against her ex-husband Rep. Max Miller on Sunday, calling for Miller to resign and seek mental health treatment.

Moreno issued a statement on Sunday only minutes after Miller himself read a statement on a live stream denying claims of abuse against his ex-wife and two-year-old daughter.

“As he has admitted privately, Max Miller needs serious psychological help. He is a danger to my daughter, and I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter,” read the senator’s statement in part. “If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them. He should not serve in the House of Representatives.”

He added: “It has been horrific to watch this play out in full public view, all while knowing an innocent two-year-old girl is caught in the middle. Our priority has always been protecting our daughter and our granddaughter. Out of concern for the safety of my family, I hoped to keep this matter private but Max Miller’s increasingly erratic and dangerous behavior has made that impossible.”

The embattled congressman is suing his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and her attorney over claims they’ve made that Miller allegedly held a gun to Emily’s head, broke his daughter’s collarbone, and engaged in drug use, as well as assaulted her by pouring hot or scalding water on her, all of which he denies.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller is suing his ex-wife for defamation while he himself faces a similar case brought by an ex-girlfriend and former Trump White House aide ( Getty )

He is separately facing a lawsuit from ex-Trump White House aide Stephanie Grisham, who dated him in 2019 and 2020 and was sued by him after she accused him, without naming him directly, of domestic abuse in a Washington Post op-ed. Grisham claims he violated the terms of a nondisclosure agreement they signed to settle that lawsuit, by claiming she was lying.

“Defendants engaged in a defamatory campaign against Plaintiff to malign his character, undermine his odds at re-election to Congress and falsely portray him as a violent and abusive father and husband,” his attorneys wrote in a court filing against Miller’s ex-wife.

Miller appeared on video to deny all allegations he faces.

"No court or agency has even substantiated any allegation against me," said the congressman. "Every single one of these allegations were already investigated."

"I'm not getting out of this race, and I'm winning in November," he continued.

Miller did not address the senator, a fellow Republican, during his own livestream. He later did so on X, writing to Moreno: “@berniemoreno If my daughter said the same thing to me, I personally wouldn’t wait two years before holding him accountable. You know this isn’t true and the only reason you are speaking out now is to hide from your own media circus. This is all political.”

Rep. Mike Turner, Miller’s colleague in the House, was asked about the situation on CBS’s Face the Nation on Sunday. Turner dodged questions about whether Republican leadership or voters should take up the issue before November, when Miller is up for re-election, and instead repeated that the allegations should be handled in “court” and not “a television studio”. He also would not answer whether the House Ethics Committee should take up an investigation into Miller’s alleged behavior.

open image in gallery Sen. Bernie Moreno called for his former son-in-law to resign from Congress on Sunday ( Getty )

open image in gallery House leadership under Mike Johnson is facing increased pressure to address the Miller allegations ( Reuters )

Republicans, including Sen. Moreno before his statement Sunday, have been facing increasing pressure to address the allegations leveled at Miller by his ex-wife and ex-girlfriend for days. The district Miller represents is a safe Republican seat but still has some on the right worried about the damage the explosive nature of the allegations could do, both as it relates to his re-election chances and those of other Republicans.

An ugly intra-party spat is the last thing Republicans need in Ohio as the state is home to a crucial Senate race this cycle and the congressional GOP caucuses are trying to protect thin dual majorities under the cloud of Donald Trump’s sinking approval ratings and dissatisfaction with Washington’s lack of focus on affordability.

A spokesperson for Emily Moreno also released a statement, responding to Miller’s livestream appearance.

“It is shameful that Max Miller decided to go on a bizarre and lie-filled rant about his ex-wife to desperately try to save his political career. There is a documented trove of evidence that Miller has a history of violent and dangerous behavior and no amount of victim shaming will change that,” said Stefan Mychajliw.

“It is despicable and abhorrent that Miller lied on an unhinged and humiliating video for their daughter to watch one day. No loving parent would have ever used their daughter as a PR pawn to save their own political career. Miller can lie and spin on X, but he cannot do so under oath in a court of law. We are confident that justice will prevail in court.”

Rumors of allegations leveled against Miller were a open secret within the GOP caucus and were openly referenced by Rep. George Santos on the House floor in 2023 during a spat with the congressman before the latter’s conviction and imprisonment on fraud charges. Miller, at the time, led an effort among Republicans to expel Santos from the House.

A crowd of critics and supporters of Indiana guard Sophie Cunningham's stance on transgender participation in women’s sports gathered around and inside Target Center on Sunday as the Fever faced the Lynx in Minnesota.

Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve wore a light blue shirt under her jacket that said, “Trans kids belong” as she coached on the bench. There were fans in the stands wearing T-shirts that read, “Trans kids belong in sports.”

It's the third straight Fever game that drew a rally after Cunningham recently voiced support for barring transgender girls and women from girls’ and women’s sports in an ESPN article published last week.

Before the game, Cunningham and Reeve held a conversation at midcourt. Cunningham appeared to be booed by the crowd on her first touch of the game.

Outside the arena, dozens of fans gathered near the entrance. A person using a loud speaker repeated over and over, “Protect trans women.” There were signs held up that read, “Love is truth" and “Thank you Sophie.”

Cunningham said Friday in Portland that she wasn't concerned about rallies against transgender participation in women’s sports becoming a distraction for the Fever.

“I think everyone who knows me personally, they know that I’m full of love. I’m bubbly. I love the people around me,” Cunningham said Friday. “I love basketball. I love inspiring the next generation and doing that in a positive light. And so that doesn’t even cross my mind. Doesn’t cross my teammates’ minds.”

Nearly three-quarters of MAGA voters would back a candidate accused of domestic violence, and two-thirds would stick with one accused of sexual assault, according to recent polling.

More broadly, most self-identified MAGA Donald Trump voters surveyed by Politico said they would stand by a GOP candidate mired in any of 12 separate scandals, including a past DUI conviction, accepting gifts from lobbyists and concealing a terminal illness.

By contrast, voters who identified as having supported Kamala Harris in 2024 were significantly less willing to indulge damaged reputations — with two notable exceptions.

The findings suggest that, for many voters, scandal is less a disqualifier than background noise, with President Trump remaining the most durable illustration of this phenomenon. He weathered political isolation after the January 6 Capitol riot, four criminal indictments and a seemingly endless catalogue of controversies so far in his second term.

“Scandal doesn’t mean what it did 15 years ago. The rules have changed, and Republican voters know it,” GOP strategist Ford O’Connell told Politico. “Republicans, particularly MAGA voters, have learned that Queensberry rules don’t win in modern politics. Today it’s a full-contact fight, more UFC than civics class, and anything goes.”

open image in gallery Most MAGA voters would back a candidate accused of domestic violence and sexual assault, according to a new poll ( Getty Images )

The poll — conducted July 13-15 with 2,061 U.S. adults — asked voters whether they would stick with their party’s candidate through 12 different scandals if the midterm elections were held tomorrow.

MAGA voters were most forgiving of candidates who used legal tax loopholes, with 82 percent saying they would still back them. Large shares also said they would support candidates who had been convicted of a DUI (76 percent), accepted gifts from lobbyists (75 percent) or been photographed wearing blackface (74 percent).

Support remained strong, though it dipped somewhat, when voters were asked about more serious allegations: 72 percent said they would back a candidate accused of domestic violence, and 66 percent said the same about one accused of sexual assault.

The smallest shares — though still majorities — said they would stand by candidates who made antisemitic comments (58 percent) or shared classified information with a foreign government (57 percent).

open image in gallery ‘Scandal doesn’t mean what it did 15 years ago. The rules have changed, and Republican voters know it,’ GOP strategist Ford O’Connell told Politico ( Getty Images )

Harris voters, meanwhile, were more generally more circumspect, with less than half saying they’d throw their support behind a Democratic candidate entangled in six of 12 scandals.

About 40 percent said they would stand by candidates accused of domestic violence or sexual assault, or those who had accepted gifts from lobbyists.

But when it came to two scandals, Harris voters were slightly more forgiving than Trump voters. Seventy percent said they would back a candidate previously convicted of a DUI, compared with 65 percent of MAGA voters. And about half said they would support an individual who made antisemitic comments — 2 percent more than MAGA voters.

open image in gallery Graham Platner, who was the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine, bowed out of the race after he was was accused last month by a former girlfriend of sexual assault, an accusation he has denied ( Reuters )

Far from being in the realm of the hypothetical, several of these scandals have played a prominent role in races across the country this year.

For instance, Graham Platner, who was the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine, was accused last month by a former girlfriend of sexual assault, following a string of other controversies. After losing the backing of key Democratic allies seemingly overnight, Platner dropped out of the race while denying the allegations.

Ohio Rep. Max Miller, who is running for re-election, has also been accused by his ex-wife of abuse, including allegations that he held a gun to her head and broke her daughter’s collarbone. Miller has denied the allegations and is suing his ex-wife.

On a livestream Sunday, Miller said, “I'm not getting out of this race, and I'm winning in November.”

That same day, his former father-in-law, Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno, issued a statement saying Miller should resign and seek mental health treatment.

“He is a danger to my daughter,” Moreno said. “If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them.”

Dikra, a 20-year-old migrant from Morocco, had spent five days in Ceuta by Sunday after swimming to the Spanish territory with her younger sister and cousin.

Since then, all her meals have come from local residents, and she isn't sure when her next one will come. Yet Dikra is certain she does not want to go back.

“I want to stay. I want to go to Spain,” Dikra said, who asked that her last name be withheld for safety reasons.

By Sunday afternoon, Dikra was among the last remaining migrants in the city after tens of thousands of the 60,000 migrants that had breached the border with Morocco on Thursday and Friday walked back to that country. At least 72 people died in the crossing, and the humanitarian crisis the sudden rush of people caused reignited a debate around immigration in Europe and beyond.

In Tangier, Dikra said she worked as a cleaner, but decided to leave alongside her sister and cousin, in part to escape her alcoholic father. She hopes to make use of a hairdressing diploma in continental Spain — from which she remains separated by the Strait of Gibraltar and the European Union's complex asylum system.

Abdel Karim, 35, also from Morocco, waited outside Ceuta's official migration reception center on Sunday, asking for updates about what officials were saying they would do with the holdouts still in the city.

Karim was unemployed in Morocco, and had lived in continental Spain years ago, before he was expelled from France where he was living on the streets.

“In Morocco, I'm seen as a deportee,” Karim said. “Those who are deported know what it means — stress, depression, anguish.”

Karim said he saw posts on social media about those making the crossing and took advantage of the chaos. He crossed with 10 euros in his pocket, he said, and pointed to his blistered feet. In Spain, Karim said he wants to do whatever work he can find, and remained unfazed about how he would get there.

Ceuta and its sister city Melilla are not part of the European Union's Schengen area, and those traveling to mainland Europe must go through border checks upon arrival.

At a beach nearby, hundreds of migrants who had arrived days earlier gathered on Sunday evening. Some crowded around an army truck where Spanish soldiers distributed water.

Senegalese migrant Cesse Aliou, 25, rested with a group of sub-Saharan men and women outside the shelter. In Morocco, Aliou said he earned 279 euros ($322) a month at a call center, but the work wasn't stable.

So he boarded a train in Casablanca to Tangier and then to Tetouan, where he said he swam to Ceuta.

Across the street, on another wooded patch near the shelter, a group of migrants began fighting over water that local residents had brought to the area.

“We are very tired. To eat, to sleep, it's very difficult here," said Aliou, pointing to the scuffle. “You see how the situation is.”

The Women’s Pro Baseball League commenced its first season Saturday as the New York Heights took on the Los Angeles Queens at Robin Roberts Stadium in Springfield, Illinois.

It was a historic game — ending in a 10-8 victory for the Queens — marking the first women’s professional baseball league in the U.S. in almost three decades.

Before that, though, the league’s big debut was nearly upstaged by a national anthem performance that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons.

Classic Motown singer Martha Reeves, 85, took to the mound to perform the “Star-Spangled Banner” alongside two other female singers.

Reeves was the lead singer of Martha and the Vandellas, who were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995.

open image in gallery The Women’s Pro Baseball League kicked off in Springfield, Illinois, on Saturday, marking the first women’s professional baseball league in the US in almost three decades ( Getty )

open image in gallery Classic Motown singer Martha Reeves’s rendition of the US National Anthem quickly went viral ( Getty )

However, Reeves’ vocals appeared very shaky as she warbled through the anthem and struggled with the song’s famous high notes.

As Reeves sang, cameras panned to the audience, many of whom were smiling or visibly struggling not to laugh. Notably, one of the actual players was seen screwing up her face in order to contain herself.

“Absolutely nothing could have prepared me for the national anthem at the first Women’s Pro Baseball League tonight,” one person captioned a clip of the performance on X, which has racked up more than three million views and 3,500 comments.

“I admire her ability to pick a key and just ignore it,” one commenter joked.

“Fergie can rest now, these women hold the throne,” wrote another, referencing the Black Eyed Peas singer’s infamous national anthem rendition at the 2018 NBA All-Star Game.

“Unfortunately, as singers age, especially women, their vocal chords thin and become more brittle. It's a tough song to sing for the best of singers, but this was just an unfortunate moment for all involved,” wrote a third in Reeves’s defence.

Someone who may be relieved to see the rendition is Patti LaBelle, who — just two weeks ago — faced ridicule for her own national anthem performance at the MLB All-Star Game.

LaBelle, 82, appeared to miss some lyrics and take some creative liberties with parts of the song, which did not go down well with fans on social media.

“Patti LaBelle is one of our greatest singers, however why people think they have to add their own twist to the National Anthem boggles my mind. Leave it alone. It was not meant to be sung with runs or ‘making it your own,’” one person on X argued after the performance.

The “Star-Spangled Banner” has a reputation for producing awkward renditions due to its exceptionally wide vocal range, treacherous melodic leaps, and the fact that it is usually performed in massive, echoey stadiums or televised globally for major sporting events.

Roseanne Barr, who famously drew criticism for her 1990 rendition, called the anthem “the hardest in the world” to sing after Ingrid Andress’s widely criticized 2024 performance.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: Man Utd may have unearthed the elusive third new central midfielder and he won’t cost Michael Carrick a penny
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED knocked down transfer enquiries for Mason Mount with Michael Carrick determined to keep him.

And his pre-season performances could present a conundrum for Ineos chiefs in the final month of the window.



Former Chelsea star Mount’s United career has been wrecked by persistent injuries since he joined for £60million in 2023.

He is now entering his fourth season at Old Trafford and arguably his most pivotal as he tries to stake a claim in Carrick’s new-look midfield.



United have spent £83m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans following Casemiro’s exit and Manuel Ugarte’s knee-ligament surgery, with a third midfielder long mooted.

But Ineos have not ruled out ending the window without a third midfielder and there is no clear frontrunner in the club’s shortlist.

United sources feel Mount is showing flashes of his former self — the player who was instrumental in Chelsea’s 2021 Champions League triumph.

Yet, we’ve heard this story before.

Mount impressed during pre-season under Ruben Amorim, who held him in high regard, only to limp off injured against Burnley in just the fourth match of the campaign.

He went on to play 90 minutes on three occasions last season, failing to start under Carrick until the penultimate game of the season against Sunderland.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Mount has been one of United’s standout performers this summer and was again the best player on the pitch in United’s 2-1 friendly win over Atletico Madrid in Sweden on Saturday.

He was again deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside £48m signing Santos for the third time this pre-season.

While Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No10, Carrick is primed to use him as a No8.

That means directly competing with Kobbie Mainoo and fellow new man Tielemans.



Ten Hag had plans for Mount to play as United’s No8 before persistent injuries stalled his career.

Unbeknownst to some, Mount was developed as a box-to-box midfielder during his Cobham youth career before Thomas Tuchel made him the inverted No10 who started the Euros final in 2021.

One United insider believes Mount’s versatility will significantly boost his prospects this season.

He combines work rate and composure with line-breaking passing, strong tackling and a natural eye for goal.

United also appear to be making an effort to promote Mount, who captained the side in the second half against Rosenborg last week and spoke to the media afterwards.



The real test is whether he can stay available long enough to demonstrate the qualities that made both Liverpool and Arsenal interested in 2023.

Carrick faces a welcome selection headache.

Mount’s resurgence in a deeper role puts him in direct competition with Mainoo and Tielemans for a starting spot.

New £35m signing and Belgium captain Tielemans is set to be involved in United’s next friendly against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg next weekend.



It will be interesting to see how all-rounder Tielemans is used against the European champs and what that means for Mount. Academy forward Shea Lacey, 19, has stood out at No10 in the last two friendlies.

Tielemans, 29, has been a class act at Aston Villa and United should have moved for him when he was a free agent in 2023 – the summer Mount joined.

United’s return to the Champions League brings a heavier fixture list — and sees Mount restored to his full £250,000-a-week salary, perhaps too much for a squad player.

With the Portsmouth native bound to Old Trafford until 2028, next summer marks United’s last chance to recoup a fee should they choose to part ways.

Mount and more defensively minded Santos, 22, have drawn headlines in a quiet pre-season.



But the ex-Chelsea pair, who arrived for a combined £110m, could soon be behind Tielemans and Mainoo in the midfield pecking order.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a huge risk not to recruit another midfielder and United still need a player who can cover distance.

Aurelien Tchouameni and Manu Kone have been linked, while Carlos Baleba has yet to fully convince everyone behind the scenes, lacking unanimous internal backing.

The final World Cup players in Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martinez, Mainoo and even Marcus Rashford are due back over the next week.

Ineos are weighing up a move for Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in their search for a left-sided player and a forward to support Benjamin Sesko, who is recovering from a shin problem.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso claims Henderson and Welbeck signings ‘more important than winning’ after shock double transfer

XABI ALONSO is not used to failure.

The new Chelsea boss won 12 major titles as a player, including a World Cup and a Euros with Spain and already has a Bundesliga and German Cup double as a manager.



Alonso, then, looks at home in the swanky presidential suite of the W Hotel overlooking Darling Harbour in Sydney, Chelsea‘s eye-catching home for the Australian leg of their pre-season tour.

Really, he should not be here at all. But it is to the Blues’ immense benefit that he is sat at the marble breakfast bar now.



It was natural that Alonso’s meteoric rise as a coach took him back to Real Madrid this time last summer.

What followed, departing in January after less than eight months in the eye of the Real storm, hurt.

But Alonso arrives at Chelsea empowered, the first to be given the title of manager under this ownership, and, he says, healed after his bruising experience in the Spanish capital.

Alonso said: “Luckily there are not too many scars in my career.

“So, OK, I got a scar. Now it is healed and now I am very motivated and determined to enjoy this next step as I did when I started in Madrid. But you move on.

“Looking back I take the positives and the things that didn’t work. I have been very critical about myself, thinking about what I could have done better because for sure it did not go as expected. But you move on to other things.

“There are many experiences, the adaptation I had to do, some things that worked and some things that didn’t in terms of the game, in terms of the man-management. It is a mixture of everything.”

The brief Madrid tenure has not dulled Alonso’s conviction or ambitions as a manager. It is a career he was destined for, ever since helping dad Periko plan his training sessions in the family kitchen in San Sebastian.

Periko managed local club Real Sociedad, where Alonso and his brother, Mikel, came through the academy, for a brief spell, though his son was on loan at Eibar at the time.

Alonso said: “He was all work. Preparing the training for the next day, preparing the team selection. That was in the kitchen and I was next to him. Did I help? I had an opinion…

“The road was not unknown for me. I had seen that at home.



“I started playing football, you become a professional, things go well, you like it, and being a midfielder, I was always curious about not just playing but why things are happening. I’m not saying it was meant to be, but I had to try it.”

The traditions of Real Sociedad, San Sebastian and the Basque Country are crucial in Alonso’s outlook and grounding as a coach.

But in the town on Spain’s north coast, while hard work and togetherness are paramount, nothing comes close to the importance of food.

So while Alonso has not found a house in London yet, it is a relief for Chelsea he has found somewhere to eat.



He said: “I was in a brasserie in Chelsea that is really close to the stadium. My wife liked it. We will have enough time [to find others].

“The Basque people, we are not obsessed, but we give a lot of importance to food and good restaurants.”

Alonso does not claim to be a stellar cook, but says his speciality is a Basque dish called Kokotxas, hake served in salsa verde.

He may not earn a Michelin star, like many from his hometown, but he was a master as a player and is working his way towards replicating that as a manager.

A visionary midfielder, Alonso played under some modern management greats and picked the brains of them all, from Carlo Ancelotti and Jose Mourinho, to Pep Guardiola and Rafa Benitez.



It was under Guardiola at Bayern Munich, in the twilight of his playing days, Alonso started to really become invested and pester the legendary boss.

He added: “We were very close. I was very curious.

“I was in that moment of my career where I could go to his office, “Pep, why is this happening? What’s going to be the game plan?” Maybe when I was 20, I didn’t have that confidence, to go to the manager’s office to ask those things.



“But at that moment, because of the trust, I needed to do that, I wanted to do that.”

That coaching education and his early success as a manager convinced Chelsea he was the man to revive them after a chaotic season.

But why, given his status, was Chelsea the right choice for him? Alonso points to his head and his gut to explain.

He said: “It had to be a lot from here, and also from here. It has to be from the guts.

“I saw it was good timing from the club, good timing for myself, a good opportunity. It is a team that has played really well recently and the situation was not as bad as it looked at the end of last season.



“There is a big potential to improve and let’s see how long it takes. I felt that I had the chance to enjoy being a manager.”

The real guarantee of enjoyment is success, and the new boss and those above him have decided they need to change in order to get there.

Deals for veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, himself a Premier League and Champions League winner, have followed Alonso’s appointment.



A blend of youth and experience was the underpinning of his invincible Leverkusen side.

He said: “You need the right balance of personalities, of maturity stages, early twenties with early thirties and in between, players in different stages of their careers.

“There’s not a formula for that, but there is a feeling for that.

“For me, this is as important as tactics. First it is the team spirit. After it is playing good football. After it is winning games.

“I felt much more responsible for the team than in my earlier years as a player.



“I wanted to not just think about myself but think about my team-mates and about how we were going to play and about supporting the young players.”

MIKEL ARTETA has ruled out a summer exit for Viktor Gyokeres amid transfer links to Spain.

Gyokeres had been touted as a potential makeweight in a deal to sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid this summer.



But the Swedish striker, who finished as Arsenal’s top scorer last season following his £63.5m move, will be staying in North London.

When asked about the future of Gyokeres, Arsenal boss Arteta simply replied: “He’s going to stay.”



Arteta refused to get drawn into any gossip about signing Alvarez too, adding: “I’m not going to talk about a footballer who isn’t ours.”

Arsenal are still exploring an ambitious deal to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid this summer, should the Brazilian not extend his current contract at the Bernabeu.

But another attacker is reminding Arteta that he already has a potential superstar in his ranks.

Teenage sensation Max Dowman scored one and set up another during the Gunners’ 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona on Saturday.

And Arteta has called on the rising star to continue his development ahead of what is likely to be a huge season for the 16-year-old.

The Arsenal manager said: “When you play for Arsenal, the expectations should be high and you should be expecting really good things.

We know what he’s capable of doing. We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver.

“But I think today he had a really good game.”

Sports.title: ‘Should never be considered again’ – Real Madrid release scathing statement on Infantino’s cancelled World Cup proposal
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID have slammed Gianni Infantino for looking to flog shares in the World Cup – and likened the bombshell proposal to LaLiga’s own commercial rights deal.

Fifa were forced to scrap plans to sell stakes in the sport’s biggest tournament after facing worldwide pressure.



And Infantino, 56, has vowed to keep his job despite the humiliating U-turn.

But Real Madrid have hit out at the Fifa supremo for wanting to allow private investors to bag a chunk of the World Cup.



The 15-time Champions League winners have released a scathing statement just 24 hours after Uefa declared a loss of confidence in Infantino.

It read: “Real Madrid welcomes Fifa’s decision to abandon its proposal for the partial sale of the commercial rights to its competitions.



“Our club believes this is good news for football, its institutions and, above all, for the millions of fans of our beloved sport.

“Real Madrid wishes to express its gratitude to Uefa, the confederations and federations, and all the institutions that firmly and responsibly opposed this project.

“Their unity and sense of duty protected football at a crucial moment. Clubs are the foundation upon which international football and the World Cup are built.

“They are the ones who discover, train, develop and provide the national teams with the players who make these major competitions possible.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“International football and the World Cup are, above all, events of public interest and they constitute a heritage that belongs to nations, fans and society as a whole.

“Therefore, we believe they should never be treated as mere financial assets to be traded for the benefit of a select few.”

Real Madrid launched civil and criminal lawsuits against LaLiga president Javier Tebas and CVC Capital Partners five years ago.

It came after the private equity firm agreed a mega-money deal with the Spanish top flight, leading to a commercial entity being created.



CVC Capital Partners received the right to more than eight per cent of the net income for 50 years.

But Real Madrid, who have appointed Jose Mourinho as their boss ahead of the new season, are set to continue challenging the partnership after an appeal was dismissed two months ago.

And Los Blancos chiefs reaffirmed their opposition while slating the World Cup plans.

The statement added: “Real Madrid firmly opposes any attempt to sell future commercial revenue from competitions without assuming any of the associated costs or risks.



“It is the clubs that bear these costs and risks, and any initiative that seeks to appropriate future football revenue without assuming the responsibilities that generate it is unacceptable and should never be considered again.

“This is also the same principle that Real Madrid has consistently upheld at the national level.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our club opposed and did not participate in the operation whereby LaLiga committed a percentage of the clubs’ future audiovisual revenues for 50 years in exchange for the entry of a private fund like CVC.

“Mortgaging for half a century revenues that belong to the clubs, who are the ones who bear all the costs and risks, sets a precedent that football must not repeat, whether in our country or internationally.”

Sports.title: Frank Lampard signs England team-mate’s son for Coventry ahead of Premier League bow
Sports.content:
FRANK LAMPARD has signed a former England team-mate’s son for Coventry City.

The Sky Blues have been bolstering their squad this summer ahead of their return to the Premier League.



The club have now added Jack Ruddy just five weeks after he left Norwich City.

The goalkeeper, 18, takes after his father John who was a stopper during his playing days.



John Ruddy, 39, starred in the Premier League for the likes of Norwich City, Wolverhampton Wanderers and Newcastle United.

He only left the Prem at the end of last season once his contract at St James’ Park expired.



Ruddy was a team-mate of Coventry boss Lampard as they were both picked for England in 2012.

They played together in the 2-1 friendly win over Italy in Bern, Switzerland.

Phil Jagielka and Jermain Defoe scored the goals for the Three Lions that day as they came from behind after Daniele De Rossi‘s opener.

Jack posed for a picture on the pitch at the Coventry Building Society Arena and it was shared on Instagram by his mum Laura.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

She wrote: “We couldn’t be prouder of you Jack! Wishing you the very best with Coventry City.

“Football isn’t always easy, and the last few years have taught you resilience, patience and how to keep believing in yourself.

“Even without the consistency and stability every young player needs to develop and thrive.

“Through it all, you’ve continued to work hard, stay focused and never lose sight of your dream.



“Now it’s time for a new beginning, fresh opportunities and, most importantly, to enjoy football again.

“Good luck Jack! We know you will give everything, as you always have, and we can’t wait to see what this next chapter brings.”

Coventry start their season with arguably the toughest test possible – against Arsenal at the Emirates on August 21.



They then host Hull City in their second league game the following weekend.



Before then, the club has pre-season friendlies against LaLiga outfit Espanyol and French giants AS Monaco.

All the latest transfer news with Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool among the Premier League teams looking to strengthen this summer

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Sunday, August 2.

The summer transfer window is full flow with several Premier League clubs beginning to ramp up their business. Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea have made a busy start to the window, while Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United loook set to follow suit.

Mikel Arteta's side look poised to make blockbuster moves for Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners have reportedly set a day aside for a medical for the Magpies' captain, with reports claiming a bid in excess of £75m has been agreed.

It's been another summer of upheaval at Newcastle United with Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon leaving St. James' Park, with Eddie Howe also leaving the club last week. Lewis Hall and Joelinton are also being linked with moves away from the club, in what would be a huge blow for incoming head coach Matthias Jaissle.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are being linked with a big money move Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions may ease their stance, however, with the signing Maghnes Akliouche and a move for Ajax winger Mika Godts.

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan
Sports.content:
Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan

Liverpool's hopes of signing PSG star Bradley Barcola have been boosted after reports suggest the French club are closing in on Ajax forward Mika Godts as his potential replacement

View 2 Images Ajax have stepped up their efforts to sign a replacement for Bradley Barcola (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly stepping up their efforts to sign Ajax star Mika Godts, which could hand Liverpool a boost to their hopes of signing Bradley Barcola. The Reds have been heavily linked with signing the France international this summer as they look to strengthen their wide forward options before the transfer window closes.

‌



Barcola’s current deal with PSG is set to expire in the summer of 2028, and it has been widely reported that the 23-year-old does not want to put pen to paper on an extension at the Parc des Princes. There have even been suggestions that Barcola is open to the idea of a move to Anfield, which has given Liverpool encouragement that a deal could be completed.

‌



It has been reported previously that Liverpool are expected to hold talks with PSG over a deal to sign Barcola, with the winger apparently valued at around £140million. That said, separate reports have suggested that Liverpool are optimistic about negotiating a fee closer to £100million for the France international.

Godts predominantly operates on the left wing for Ajax, and should the deal go through, it would probably fuel additional suggestions that Barcola might be heading towards the exit. PSG are also understood to be nearing a deal to bring in Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco, which would further fuel the speculation that Barcola could end up departing the Ligue 1 champions.

Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut

Alejandro Garnacho has completed a loan move from Chelsea to Aston Villa and the former Manchester United winger has appeared to take a dig at his former employers

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho left Chelsea for Aston Villa (Image: Chelsea Football Club, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Alejandro Garnacho has claimed he is enjoying football again in an apparent dig at former club Chelsea. The Argentinian made his Aston Villa debut against Indonesia All Stars as Unai Emery's side ran out 3-1 winners but the 22-year-old couldn't resist a swipe at the Blues.

‌



Garnacho joined the Europa League holders on a season-long loan with a conditional obligation to buy for £43million, should Villa opt to trigger it. It appears no love has been lost with his former employers after suggesting he had an unhappy time at Stamford Bridge.

‌



Xabi Alonso made the attacker surplus to requirements after being appointed as the permanent manager. Garnacho, who left Manchester United under a cloud last summer, has sparked another bitter dispute after departing a club.

‌



Taking to social media following their 3-1 victory over Indonesia All Stars, Garnacho said: "First start after three months.

Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

"Happy to be enjoying football again. One percent every day. Thanks Indonesia."

The attacker's stint at Old Trafford concluded on a bitter note before his initial switch to Stamford Bridge failed to come off in January 2025. Garnacho lost favour under Ruben Amorim and was dropped from the squad for the victory over Manchester City, while his omission from the Europa League final starting XI prompted a post-match outburst.

‌



United will be monitoring developments closely as Garnacho prepares for his maiden season in the West Midlands. Michael Carrick's outfit would be entitled to 10 per cent of any future transfer fee for the 22-year-old and should the buyout clause be activated, Villa will be obliged to pay £43million for his signature.

Garnacho endured a torrid debut season in the capital, during a chaotic period for the Londoners that saw a string of managerial changes. Liam Rosenior was subsequently appointed as his replacement, yet his time in charge proved brief, with the axe falling after just 106 days

Emery now faces the task of reviving Garnacho's career after a bruising spell at both United and Chelsea. The Europa League-winning manager said: "We are delighted with Alejandro. He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy."

Sports.title: 10th-tier side release bizarre Jadon Sancho statement as Man Utd flop looks for new club
Sports.content:
10th-tier side release bizarre Jadon Sancho statement as Man Utd flop looks for new club

Jadon Sancho has been training by himself since being released by Manchester United at the end of June and his latest move has prompted a non-league side to release a statement

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho has been training at Flixton FC (Image: PA)

Non-league side Flixton have felt compelled to release a statement stating that Jadon Sancho is not in talks to sign for them after speculation on social media.

‌



Sancho is currently a free agent, having been released by Manchester United on July 1. The 26-year-old left the club alongside Casemiro and Tyrell Malacia and is yet to find a new team in the summer transfer window.

‌



His £73million transfer from Borussia Dortmund did not work out at Old Trafford, with just 12 goals coming in 83 appearances over the past five years. Sancho spent time on loan with Borussia Dortmund and Chelsea before playing last season with Aston Villa.

‌



With no club, Sancho has taken to training solo at Flixton FC in Greater Manchester. In a video for the 10th-tier club's social media channels he praised their facilities, leading to some tongue-in-cheek speculation that he could drop down to non-league.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“You’ve got a nice layout here," Sancho said. “It’s my first time around this area, and it's the first time I’ve seen a nice pitch [in this area] apart from United and City."

‌



The club, who have Rhodri Giggs - the brother of United legend Ryan as their assistant manager - have decided to clarify the situation. In a statement, Flixton owner Christopher Garcia said: "Over the past few days, we've seen a number of posts and comments circulating regarding Jadon Sancho's visit to Flixton FC.

"To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions. He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.

"We're proud that the quality of our pitch and facilities made Flixton a place where a player of his calibre felt comfortable training, and he is welcome to train at Flixton FC whenever he wishes.

‌



View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is looking for a new club (Image: PA)

"During his visit, Jadon was nothing but professional, humble, and generous with his time. After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

"Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of. He deserves respect for both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.

‌



"We thank Jadon for choosing Flixton FC as a place to train and wish him every success in the next stage of his career, which will undoubtedly be at a level far above where we currently compete. Our doors will always be open to him."

Sancho is yet to field much interest in his services, with Qatari side Al-Rayyan one of few to make an enquiry. The winger is said to be open to moving to the Middle East, where the Saudi Pro League is a possibility, or staying in Europe.

Sports.content:
Preston vs Barcelona friendly cancelled hours before kick-off for bizarre reason

Preston North End's pre-season friendly with Barcelona has been cancelled at the 11th hour, with the Championship side set to face the Spanish giants in a behind-closed-doors match at St. George's Park

View 2 Images Barcelona are in the United Kingdom for pre-season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Barcelona's pre-season friendly against Prest North End has been called off just one day before it was meant to take place. The La Liga giants were scheduled to face the Championship side in a behind-closed-doors friendly at St. George's Park.

‌



Hansi Flick's side are currently in the United Kingdom preparing for the new season, and played Birmingham City last week, losing the match on penalties. The hope of being able to get another intense runout in for Karim Adeyemi and co, while much of the squad is yet to return from their break following the World Cup, failed to come to fruition, however.

‌



Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Preston were unwilling to risk more senior stars for the match and instead proposed a game with their under-21 squad, being unable to fill the places for a full senior squad. The suggestion was declined by Barca, who have decided to hold a normal training session in its place.

‌



Preston take on Huddersfield Town in the League Cup in the coming days and were not willing to risk further injuries as a result. Barcelona will soon return to Spain, earlier than planned, to continue their preparations.

They will take on British opposition, with two further pre-season matches lined up against Udinese and Nottingham Forest next weekend. Flick's side will travel to Italy to play in the three-team tournament, with three 45-minute matches taking place at the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine.

Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is set to leave Old Trafford this summer, with the Turkey international expected to join La Liga side Celta Vigo on a loan deal

View 2 Images Michael Carrick faces a busy summer as Manchester United manager (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Altay Bayindir is getting closer to completing a move away from Manchester United this summer. La Liga club Celta Vigo are set to sign the Turkey international.

‌



United signed Bayindir from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, but the shot-stopper has made just 17 appearances during his three years at Old Trafford. Bayindir joined United to serve as the understudy to Andre Onana, which was the case for his first two years at the club.

‌



That changed last summer when Senne Lammens signed for the Red Devils and went on to become the club’s new No.1 goalkeeper. Bayindir's prospects at United have been shrouded in doubt for quite some time, particularly following the club's decision to bring in Karl Darlow on a free transfer earlier this summer.

‌



Man Utd star claims club can win Premier League after mood change under Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

It has now been reported by Metropolitano that Celta Vigo are on the brink of signing Bayindir on a loan basis from United, with the deal said to be almost entirely wrapped up in quick fashion. The same report suggests that the La Liga club are hopeful of formally announcing the agreement to sign Bayindir next week, with the goalkeeper anticipated to join his new squad at a training camp in Italy.

A separate report from Spanish publication AS claims that the 28-year-old is expected to undergo a medical to complete his move to Celta Vigo on either Sunday or Monday. Our sister title The Manchester Evening News reported on Saturday that Celta Vigo are leading the chase to secure Bayindir's signature, with the goalkeeper appearing increasingly likely to depart the club in the coming days.

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir looks to be on his way out of Old Trafford (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Sports.title: 5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job
Sports.content:
5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job

Gianni Infantino's job security as FIFA president has taken a huge blow following the major backlash towards his controversial plans - and efforts are being made to oust him

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is reportedly reluctant to challenge Gianni Infantino

Gianni Infantino's days as FIFA president appear to be numbered after his plans to sell stakes in tournaments to investors backfired spectacularly.

‌



Infantino clearly misjudged the reaction to his secretive plot and could pay for the mistake with his job. UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation all voiced their displeasure with the plans, forcing Infantino to perform a humiliating U-turn.

‌



But his opponents are not satisfied with having killed the plot; they want Infantino gone following 10 years at the top of world football. UEFA are said to be 'accelerating' plans to remove the Swiss and FIFA insiders believe he is now 'certain' to go.

‌



If Infantino doesn't resign, then his opponents may have to force a vote of no confidence in his leadership, or back a rival in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. So who could put their name forward by November 18 to succeed Infantino in the election next year?

As the chiefs of world football scheme away behind the scenes, Mirror Football takes a look at five possible contenders.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Victor Montagliani

The Canadian is the CONCACAF president and has emerged as one of the main contenders in a chaotic past few days. CONCACAF rejected FIFA's proposal for private investment, but was less critical in its words than UEFA.

Montagliani is a long-time ally of Infantino's but is reportedly ready to stand against him in the elections. Before the scandal, the 60-year-old was not going to challenge Infantino - who had been set to run unopposed - but had an eye on going for the role in 2031.

Yet Infantino's sudden unpopularity has seen Montagliani sense an opportunity with his involvement in the World Cup boosting his profile and credentials. He was the first non-Caribbean CONCACAF president since 1969 when he took over and is said to have support beyond his own federation.

‌



View 4 Images CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is one of the contenders (Image: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images)

Nasser al-Khelaifi

The Paris Saint-Germain president is one of the most powerful figures in football. The Qatari leads the European Football Clubs umbrella group and is extremely influential in European club football.

Al-Khelaifi has plenty of allies and has been suggested as the next FIFA president. The only problem is that he is reportedly not keen, with a source saying he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, nor any interest in this role at FIFA".

‌



The chances of him changing his mind now appear even less likely after the Qatar Football Association put out a statement backing Infantino on Sunday.

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is a powerful figure in European football (Image: LOU BENOIST/AFP via Getty Images)

Mattias Granstrom

Granstrom is the FIFA general secretary and is seen as the most likely internal candidate to step up and replace Infantino. While he lacks the profile of the other candidates, he has reportedly not been tarnished by Infantino's plan and could therefore garner support, were he to consider running.

‌



Dariusz Mioduski

The Polish lawyer is currently the vice-president of the European Football Clubs body, as well as president and owner of Legia Warsaw. His name has come up in the swirling rumour mill of the past few days

Mioduski has been backed by the Belgian, Spanish, Norwegian, German and Swedish associations, according to a report from talkSPORT earlier this month. With UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin reportedly unwilling to challenge for the FIFA presidency, Mioduski could become the European candidate.

View 4 Images Dariusz Mioduski has supporters in Europe (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sheikh Salman bin E brahim Al Khalifa

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president is another possible candidate, despite initial reluctance to step forward. The AFC released a statement saying it "stands in solidarity" with UEFA and CONCACAF, but their words were much less fiery and there is reportedly less conviction in the territory's opposition to Infantino's plans.

Al Khalifa is a Bahraini and is very experienced, having been in charge of the AFC since 2013. But it remains to seen whether the 60-year-old wants to put his name forward.

Sports.title: Blue Bolt confirms superiority over Precise at Deauville
Sports.content:
Blue Bolt continued her faultless campaign with victory in the Prix Rothschild at Deauville.

Runner-up to Fallen Angel in the Sun Chariot at Newmarket at the end of last season, Andrew Balding's filly has taken her game to another level this term with a comeback win in Listed company at Goodwood followed by big-race triumphs in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Falmouth at Newmarket.

The four-year-old was renewing rivalry with the July course runner-up, Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes heroine Precise, and at one stage it looked like the latter may take her revenge in the hands of Ryan Moore.

But Blue Bolt was doing her best work at the finish under Colin Keane and lunged late to claim a seventh win from 10 career starts, with Sir Mark Prescott's Coronation Stakes fourth Moon Target bettering that result with a fine effort to finish third.

Balding told Sky Sports Racing: "She's some filly, she really is - and Colin gave her a wonderful ride. It wasn't very comfortable watching it, I thought we were beat in the last furlong, but he's judged it to perfection.

"She's got great physical strength for a filly, that's her biggest quality, and she's got great desire as well. A big thank you to the team at home and Alfie Redman who rides her every day. She's not easy and likes to take control of things, but he's really mastered her this last six months and done a great job of it.

"She likes to get on with it, she's a powerful traveller and knows her strength, so it's about harnessing that in the right direction."

Blue Bolt now looks set to bid for further Group One success in Ireland, with her trainer adding: "The great thing about her is she's effective on any ground, which is a big help.

"We always felt the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (September 12) was her race this year and we won't lose sight of that for anything prior to that."

Sports.title: Dunkley leads Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds as MI London remain winless
Sports.content:
Sophia Dunkley's 56 off 33 balls fired Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds in an impressive victory by five runs in The Hundred at Trent Bridge.

Opener Dunkley's imperious innings was aided by a useful contribution from her international team-mate Nat Sciver-Brunt (33 off 25) and a cameo from Bess Heath to leave the Rockets with a middling - but defendable - score of 139-7 after their 100 balls.

Australia star Ash Gardener (1-18) delivered for the home side, taking the early wicket of opener Bryony Smith (10 off 12) and limiting the top-order scoring of Jess Jonassen (19 off 18) and Phoebe Litchfield (24 off 22) to leave SunRisers Leeds well behind the required run-rate at 73-3 off 64 balls.

Image: Phoebe Litchfield managed 24 off 22 before being dismissed by Charley Phillips

Annabel Sutherland, though, reignited hope for the batting side with a brilliant 59no off 30 deliveries, but it was too little too late for the visitors as some tidy bowling by Kim Garth (0-26) at the death - despite a last-ball maximum by Sutherland - meant the Rockets held on and secured an important victory.

The win consolidates their strong position as they remain second in the table, while SunRisers Leeds, languishing in seventh, take another damaging blow to their Eliminator chances.

Manchester Super Giants leave MI London winless

Manchester Super Giants consolidated their third-place position in The Hundred with a six-wicket win over MI London.

MI London, still without a win and planted firmly at the foot of the table, lost the toss and were asked to bat, and it was imperative that they got off to a decent start in the absence of Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who has been ruled out the remainder of the tournament.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Blue Bolt and Precise clash again in Prix Rothschild
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Sunday with Flat action from Chester, Yarmouth and Deauville, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.40 Deauville - Star fillies Blue Bolt and Precise lock horns again

A red-hot renewal of this Group One Prix Rothschild at Deauville where Blue Bolt and Precise renew their rivalry.

Andrew Balding's Blue Bolt saw off Precise when landing a first Group One success in the Falmouth at Newmarket last month and bids to confirm that form under Colin Keane. A dominant winner on that occasion, the market believes she can follow up and land a four-timer.

Balding said: "She seems in good nick and if she repeats the performance from Newmarket she will take a lot of beating.

"She's been a star this year and the only factor is she has never travelled far from home to run before. But if she takes the travel in her stride then she should hold every chance of continuing her winning run."

Aidan O'Brien saddles Precise, herself a four-time Group One scorer, with Ryan Moore in the plate. An impressive winner of the Irish 1000 Guineas, she took the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot before failing to land a blow on Blue Bolt. Sent off the odds-on favourite that day, it will be fascinating to see if she can reverse the form.

O'Brien said: "She's in good form, she was stood in the gates a little bit long the last day and lost a couple of lengths and turned her head a little bit.

"Hopefully she won't do that the next day and give away those lengths. It's hard to do that at somewhere like Newmarket, especially at the July meeting where you are going straight down. We're happy with everything she's doing and looking forward to seeing her again, she's been a special filly for us so far."

Moon Target has two lengths to find on her fourth behind Precise at the Royal meeting, while Green Spirit might appreciate the drop back to a mile.

A deep contest has several with each-way claims including Karl Burke's 1,000 Guineas runner-up Evolutionist.

3.20 Chester - Unbeaten Lifeplan heads the field

Declan Carroll's Lifeplan faces eight rivals as he bids to remain unbeaten in a cracking edition of the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester.

Last year's Gimcrack champion has not been seen since landing that prestigious prize back in August and his connections are hoping he can make up for lost time. Stall nine will make life a bit trickier for jockey Zak Wheatley however.

Song Of The Clyde is a top performer on his day and showed all his ability when taking the Listed Carnarvon Stakes at Newbury. Below his best the last twice, he will not want conditions to be too quick.

Hugo Palmer fields Fitzella and Ardisia who are both closely matched on the pick of their runs, while Calico Blue steps up in class for Roger Varian.

12.56 Deauville - Woot Woot, Nicely and Queen Of The Day clash

A strong edition of the Sky Sports Racing Prix Six Perfections where a host of in-form two-year-old clash over seven furlongs.

Christopher Head has never hidden his admiration for Woot Woot and she justified that reputation when winning impressively at Saint-Cloud and she warrants respect on this grade.

Queen Of The Day defeated Woot Woot on debut before chasing home the exciting Avec Toi on her second start and she will find this an easier task.

British raider Nicely stepped forward from her debut to win comfortably at Hamilton and adds further intrigue to this splendid opener.

Best of the rest

3.05 Deauville - Group Three where Elle Eclipse and Lefteye feature. Evita has good form behind Diamond Necklace. William Buick rides Symbol Of Majesty.
