Sports.title: Andoni Iraola reveals why his Liverpool coach rejected EFL jobs this summer
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola says assistant Tommy Elphick's Liverpool support convinced him not to take a Championship job this summer.

Iraola is continuing his preparations to lead Liverpool into the new season after succeeding Arne Slot in the Anfield dugout.



2 Iraola signed a two-year contract as Liverpool's new head coach Credit: Getty

And he's brought with him to Merseyside two of his colleagues from Bournemouth, who he guided to an historic seventh-placed Premier League finish last season.

Elphick and Shaun Cooper, both Bournemouth legends as players, were coaching at the club when Iraola arrived in 2023 and have followed him to his next job in charge of the Reds.

And Iraola is glad to have them with him, telling Liverpool club media: "Yes, for me, Tommy and Shaun are very valuable because they have been English players, they’ve played in the Premier League, the Championship, League One; they understand the culture, they understand what the players are thinking.



"And they’ve gone through the process of understanding how to build a team, because we didn’t know each other when I arrived at Bournemouth and they have seen all the process during these three years where we’ve been evolving, we’ve been adding different things.

"So now, I think they are the best ones to transmit the same thing to the players and to the new coaches, that we already had in the club. They are helping me a lot.



"I think they are sometimes in more touch with the players than me because always with the manager there is a little bit of more distance, I think the players are more comfortable sometimes with the assistants.

"They know also when to filter the information – when I need to know things. Sometimes they don’t tell me the things that for sure stay between them and the players. They are brilliant in this."



Who could Elphick have joined?

Iraola might have lost Elphick this summer, as he explained: "Tommy, I tell him, he is living his dream. I think he had this summer a chance to coach in the Championship. Good clubs called him, but I think he couldn’t miss this because he’s been a big Liverpool fan.

"We were talking the other day, meeting with the legends we have here, with Robbie Fowler, Ian Rush – he was like, ‘Oof, this is big.’ I like how he is feeling it and I think it’s very nice for him, yes."

Elphick held talks with Bristol City over his first senior role in management.

2 Elphick worked under Iraola at Bournemouth Credit: AFP



Despite the 38-year-old being impressed with the Robins' plans, he decided against the move.

Burnley were also believed to have shown interest in Elphick.

Liverpool beat Wrexham 1-0 in New York in their latest pre-season friendly on Thursday.

The Reds round off their US tour by taking on Leeds in Chicago on Sunday night, before home friendlies against Monaco and Como.

They begin the new Premier League campaign away to Newcastle on August 23 then meet Nottingham Forest in their home opener six days later.



Liverpool fell short in the defence of their Premier League crown last term, finishing fifth – and while that was enough to clinch Champions League qualification, their performance ultimately cost title-winning boss Slot his job.

Iraola is one of eight confirmed new Premier League managers for 2026/27.

That number will rise to nine after Eddie Howe stepped down as Newcastle boss on Friday.

The Magpies are expected to appoint Al-Ahli head coach Matthias Jaissle as Howe's successor.

Sports.title: Argentinian star signs for Chelsea, Newcastle's £27m goalkeeping target completes medical, Bournemouth bag Sevilla ace - while Hull are set to beat Rangers and Cardiff City to highly-rated Norwegian: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Blues sign England nemesis

Chelsea have completed the signing of Argentina midfielder Valentin Barco from sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year contract.

The 22-year-old stirred controversy when his over-zealous celebrations of Argentina's victory over England at the World Cup provoked an angry reaction from Jude Bellingham.

Barco, who previously made six Premier League appearances for Brighton, has been signed following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid earlier this summer but he has been playing in midfield.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in May, he left for Chelsea at the end of the season, saying his farewells to Strasbourg supporters.

Chelsea are also continuing negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Chelsea have completed the signing of England World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco (right)

Tractor Boys close in on new midfielder

Ipswich Town are closing in on the £16million signing of Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, the Portuguese midfielder was leaning towards a move to Portman Road after they declared their interest even though Hull City had been in advanced talks over an initial loan for the 26-year-old.

However, Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic revealed over the weekend that they were set to miss out to a club that was willing to sign him on a permanent deal.

Newcastle's new No 1 completes medical ahead of transfer

Goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek has completed his Newcastle United medical in Spain, and is set to be announced as the club’s latest signing.

Newcastle activated his £25.7m release clause and the player travelled to La Manga on Saturday.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, the 24-year-old Czech is being brought in as the club’s new first-choice option in goal.

Lukas Hornicek has completed his medical ahead of joining Newcastle in a £25.7million deal

Bournemouth bolster full-back options

Bournemouth have agreed an £11.2m deal with Sevilla for right-back Juanlu Sanchez.

The deal is worth £9.5m plus a potential £1.7m in add-ons while Sevilla retain a 10 per sell-on.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday, Bournemouth accelerated talks as they needed a right-back after the departure of Alex Jimenez to Fiorentina.

The 22-year-old Juanlu is a Spain international with four caps and had interest from Everton.

Wigan chasing Chelsea starlet

Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh is wanted on loan at Wigan Athletic.

The two clubs recently did business together when Chelsea completed the transfer of highly-rated 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan on a four year contract.

Walsh became Chelsea’s youngest player to feature in the Champions League last season and will be hoping to build on his senior breakthrough during the 2026-27 campaign.

He figured briefly in the friendly defeat to Spurs in the Sydney Cup and was among several academy players involved as Xabi Alonso took charge of his first training session, alongside senior players such as Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

Walsh has returned to pre-season looking physically bigger and stronger so Chelsea are keen to see how he copes with more competitive game time.

Hammers chase former Spurs star

West Ham have joined the clubs showing interest in AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott.

Como, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis have already made enquiries.

The former Tottenham academy graduate is in demand after scoring 31 goals last season.

Alkmaar though are reluctant to sell the 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international to a rival Dutch club.

West Ham have entered the race to sign former Tottenham forward Troy Parrott

Hull lead race for Norwegian star

Hull City are ready to fend off interest from Rangers and Cardiff City to sign highly-rated Norwegian midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl.

Cardiff had offered a club record fee for the 20-year-old from Tromso but Hull are offering him the chance to play in the Premier League.

The 6ft 4ins defensive midfielder has captained Norway at youth level and is an U21 international.

Hull are also advancing in talks for 18-year-old centre back Lucas Herrington from Colorado Rapids and winger Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.

Sports.title: England's World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco joins Chelsea: Argentina star who provoked Three Lions in semi-final defeat confirms switch to Stamford Bridge after Atlanta antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

Barco, 22, who can play in midfield and at left-back, joins the Blues from their sister club Strasbourg.

The Argentine hit the headlines last month when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco made just one substitute appearance at the tournament, but he infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove.

Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco clashed with Jude Bellingham after Argentina's semi-final victory over England

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

Given his involvement in the World Cup, Barco won't join up with his new team-mates until later in pre-season.

The versatile star began his career back home with Boca Juniors, making his debut at the age of 16.

After impressing in Argentina, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for £7.4million yet he struggled to establish himself on the south coast, and spent time on loan at Sevilla and Strasbourg.

He joined Strasbourg permanently in July 2025 and was regularly linked with a move away after impressing in France, where his side qualified for Europe.

Barco contributed 12 goals and assists last season and his strong form saw him earn a place in Argentina's World Cup squad, although he played just 19 minutes in a group stage victory over Jordan.

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

His arrival at Stamford Bridge comes following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid, although Chelsea are still in negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Barco is the Blues' seventh signing of the summer, with Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and former Strasbourg striker Emmanuel Emegha all also joining the club.

He has similarly become the 13th player to move between the French side and Chelsea since BlueCo took over Strasbourg in 2023, a year after they purchased the Premier League side.

Sports.title: Argentina's Valentin Barco earned a slap from Jude Bellingham and will feel the heat from English fans when he kicks off his Chelsea career... but here's how his talent can win over his petulance
Sports.content:
It has been just over a fortnight since Argentina beat England in their World Cup semi-final grudge match, and it is fair to say the English are still feeling the heartache.

The pain of a late defeat was exacerbated by the taunting nature of the Argentine celebrations, as were several displays of clear aggression and petulance from the Albiceleste during their late reprise and eventual victory in Atlanta.

Perhaps one of the more memorable aspects of this provocative Argentine behaviour were the actions of Chelsea-bound Valentin Barco, whose move to Stamford Bridge was confirmed on Sunday evening.

The Blues’ latest acquisition, 22, will expect a hostile welcome to the Premier League by the vast majority of fans as a result of his antics in the semi-final.

Despite not playing in the match, the former Strasbourg man was unsportsmanlike to say the least in his celebration of Enzo Fernandez’s late equaliser, resulting in a bust-up with Three Lions hero Jude Bellingham, who slapped him on the back of the head after the game.

Jude Bellingham clashed with unused Argentina substitute Valentin Barco

Barco's provocative celebrations irked England's star man after their semi final clash

Bellingham delivered a slap on the back of the head for the defender, who is set to join Chelsea

Barco started this by bounding across the pitch and through a number of dejected English players after Fernandez’s effort flew past Jordan Pickford, with the substitute having no acceptable reason for being so far on the field of play.

While Barco clearly succeeded in his attempts to rattle Tuchel’s team, he may not have thought through the possible consequences.

Bellingham's relatively tame slap will most likely not be the final punishment the youngsterwill receive. With Barco joining Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in Ligue 1, one would imagine there may be some awkwardness with his new skipper Reece James and Chelsea's other English stars.

Perhaps, though, they will put it all to one side as they band together ahead of the new Premier League season. If so, the Argentine’s biggest concern should be the reception he can expect from opposing fans, as well as perhaps other members of the doomed England team.

Barco will, of course, have the opportunity to silence his critics with his ability on the pitch. The young man can look to the example set by outgoing Chelsea star Marc Cucurella, who was in a similar position to the full-back just two years ago.

Off the back of Euro 2024 final, when his Spain side beat England 2-1, the left back was the subject of major derision and hatred from the English press and supporters alike due to his antics during the game and in the post-match celebrations.

Cucurella himself said he thought he was being treated more harshly by the authorities, saying they were 'going after' him as 'they're hurt'.

However, two years later he leaves England for Real Madrid having earned respect through his excellent performances at Stamford Bridge.

But matching the Spaniard’s trajectory will not be easy for Barco, partly because the Boca Juniors academy graduate has failed to impress before in the Premier League, during his stint at Brighton.

Barco featured as a substitute in the group-stage win over Jordan but did not play in any of Argentina's other seven matches at the World Cup

His underwhelming performances on the south coast were characterised mainly by an inability to deal with the pace and physicality of the division, a common obstacle for foreign imports in the Premier League. But what was more worrying was the surprisingly small amount of quality he displayed on the ball, as ever since he first gained attention from European clubs at a very young age he has always been viewed as extremely technically gifted.

However, in spite of this disappointing spell at Brighton, he found his footing in France and quickly became a key figure in Liam Rosenior’s 2024-25 Strasbourg side.

In Ligue 1, the Argentinian regained confidence and enjoyed a great run of form in the season just gone under Liam Rosenior and eventually Gary O’Neil, which ultimately earned him a place in Lionel Scaloni’s 2026 World Cup squad. Barco played an impressive 43 games for Strasbourg in all competitions last season, registering three goals and six assists.

Barco has joined Chelsea after making a name for himself for all the wrong reasons

As a result, Barco has become the latest Strasbourg player to have earned a move from North France to West London in the BlueCo era, and despite a lot of Chelsea fans being sceptical about the move, one does have to concede that he seems to be a perfect fit for new manager Alonso’s dynamic back-three system.

This is partially due to the diminutive Argentinian’s positional versatility. Barco has previously been deployed as a left back in a back four, a left wing back in a back five as well as most recently coming into his own as a left sided defensive midfielder in a double pivot.

This, along with his work-rate on the pitch, sharp footballing brain and wicked left foot have earned Barco a lot of recent attention from modern attack-minded managers, such as the new Chelsea boss who now has another excellent option in his new squad for the upcoming season.

However, currently his petulant behaviour overshadows his ability and puts any fanfare surrounding the signing on hold. Barco will have to be aware of and prepare himself for the constant abuse he is likely to receive from English fans next season.

It will be fascinating to see how the young talent responds to this inevitable criticism and how it may affect how he performs for his new club.

Sports.title: Donald Trump wins golf tournament with barely-believable score at his own course... after 'disrespectful' faux pas in front of US troops
Sports.content:
Donald Trump has added two more trophies to his collection after winning both the club and senior championships at his golf course in New Jersey this weekend.

Trump, 80, carded an improbably low 2-under-par score of 70 at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster over the weekend, bringing his reported tally to over 40 total victories across his various golf properties.

Social media footage showed the US President receiving a round of applause in front of the club leaderboard following the round, with a caption confirming he had collected two trophies for his performance.

The par at Bedminster is set at 72, meaning Trump allegedly finished two strokes under par to secure the double victory.

The reported 70 comes a year after the White House published a scorecard claiming Trump had carded a 3-under 69 at the same annual tournament in 2025 to win by 10 gross strokes.

Trump was seen visiting troops during his trip to New Jersey, though observers noted he was still wearing his golf glove while greeting military personnel.

Donald Trump has added two more trophies to his collection after winning both the club and senior championships at his golf course in New Jersey this weekend

Trump allegedly just won his 43rd Club Championship today at one of his courses. pic.twitter.com/8Lb8GFvnY0 — Ron Filipkowski (@RonFilipkowski) August 2, 2026

'With his golf glove on. How disrespectful,' one X user wrote in response to a video.

Another added, 'He wears his golf shoes and driving glove wherever he goes, I'm guessing....???'

The avid golfer has consistently touted his prowess on the course, declaring: 'I've played a lot, and I've played well. There are very few people who can beat me in golf.'

However, his remarkable track record and reported scores have frequently drawn skepticism from critics and sports journalists over the years.

Sportswriter Rick Reilly, who authored a book on Trump's golf habits, has previously questioned the legitimacy of his club championship wins, once stating: 'When it comes to cheating, he's an 11 on a scale of one to 10.'

Trump's outing on the course comes shortly after he said he has called off strikes on Iran 'subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL' with the Islamic regime.

The president said on Truth Social on Saturday evening that although he remains 'locked and loaded' to launch an attack, he halted the strikes in hopes of reaching a peace deal.

Trump's announcement came after reports claimed he was talked down by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over concerns that further strikes could dramatically escalate the conflict in the Middle East.

Sources told Axios that the Crown Prince urged Trump to defuse the situation, following days of tit-for-tat threats between the White House and Tehran.

Trump, 80, carded a 2-under-par score of 70 at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster

Trump visits U.S. troops in New Jersey.pic.twitter.com/fZfAZINSAS — Clash Report (@clashreport) August 1, 2026

In Trump's Truth Social post on Saturday night, he threatened to unleash 'power not seen since World War II,' but said he agreed to tentatively pause the attack.

'We have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,' Trump wrote.

'This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat.

'Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL. The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment.'

Sports.title: Chelsea's new manager Xabi Alonso on how he 'reset' after the 'scar' Real Madrid disaster, the importance of signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - and why he thinks the Blues is the right move
Sports.content:
Chelsea's new manager Xabi Alonso on how he 'reset' after the 'scar' Real Madrid disaster, the importance of signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - and why he thinks the Blues is the right move

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

We are up above Down Under with Xabi Alonso, looking out over the Darling Harbour from the 27th floor of the W Sydney hotel in the appropriately-named Extreme Wow penthouse suite.

There are worse settings than this ultra-luxurious 202sqm space for Alonso to be feeling a little jet-lagged, and he starts by telling us how he has made the most of his early morning wake-ups between 2am and 6am. He completed a 10km run - at four minutes and 30 seconds per km, a highly respectable speed at 44 years old - before we begin discussing something else which flew by.

That is the seven months he spent as manager of Real Madrid, whose loss will hopefully be Chelsea's gain. 'Luckily there are not too many scars in my career,' Alonso tells us.

'So, OK, I got a scar, but this heals. Now it is healed and now I am very motivated and determined to enjoy this next step, as I did when I started in Madrid. You move on.

'Looking back, I take the positives and the things that didn't work. I have been very critical about myself, thinking about what I could have done better, because for sure it did not go as expected. But you move on to other things.'

To bigger and better things, hopefully, now that he is in charge of Chelsea in the Premier League. He is a hell of a hire by their BlueCo owners, as good as an appointment that they could have secured after the hiring and firing of Liam Rosenior last season.

Xabi Alonso has opened up about becoming Chelsea manager and what drew him into joining

He was sacked just months into becoming Real Madrid boss last term - which he calls a 'scar'

Having now 'reset', the 44-year-old is now in charge of Chelsea - having joined this summer

Moving his finger from his head to his stomach as we talk taking over Chelsea, Alonso continues: 'It had to be a lot from here, and also from here, from the guts. It was good timing. Good timing for the club. Good timing for myself.

'This is a team that played really well recently. The situation was not as bad as it looked at the end of last season. There is big potential. Let's see how long it takes. We are in that process. I felt that I had the chance to enjoy being a manager.'

Sydney is just the first stop on Chelsea's pre-season tour. Next, Alonso will be in Hong Kong, then Indonesia, then Malaysia, playing one friendly in each country before returning to England.

Alonso is not actually staying in the Extreme Wow suite. We have just borrowed it for this sit-down with Chelsea's new manager. There is a bottle of Castaneda 1965 Bas-Armagnac to our right, but if we open it, it will set us back $950 (£497) with our Australian hotel hosts. It feels like a space fit for a super villain, and Alonso is too nice for that. He screams emotional intelligence.

'I used my time to reset the energy because you need to be full of energy as a manager to pull from the rest,' Alonso continues.

'It is very important for me to transmit this passion, this enthusiasm for the game in every training session, every game plan. I used that time mainly for that. I didn't watch much football. It was mainly about myself, about feeling it. You learn from the disappointment of things that were not meant to be and you think things will be better.'

Alonso arrived at Chelsea believing he knew what was needed. They are used to having the youngest side in the Premier League. Now they have completed deals for Danny Welbeck, 35 and from Brighton, and Jordan Henderson, 36 and from Brentford. While the fee for Welbeck is currently undisclosed, he is believed to have cost next to nothing, while Henderson is a free transfer as his club allowed him to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected. Together, they will add 863 Premier League games' worth of experience to this youthful squad.

'For me, you need the right balance of personalities, of maturity stages, early 20s with early 30s and in between, players in different stages of their careers,' Alonso says when asked for the ingredients to a winning culture. 'There's not a formula for that, but there is a feeling for that.

Danny Welbeck (left) and Jordan Henderson will bring veteran nous to the Blues this season

'If they have good qualities and good interaction between them, you create good connections and good bonds between them and that helps the team spirit. For me, this is as important as tactics. First it is the team spirit. After it is playing good football. After it is winning games.

'I learned this from playing football. "I love playing with this team". You could feel it. For me, it's very natural. In the Basque Country, we have a lot of that collective purpose, that culture.'

Alonso had that at Bayer Leverkusen, where he did the Double in 2023-24, winning the Bundesliga for the first time in their history as well as the DFB-Pokal. They also finished Europa League runners-up. The Spaniard prioritises the best people over the best players, and adds on his time at Leverkusen while smiling: 'It was unexpectedly fantastic.'

Alonso is not trying to mimic one of his old legendary managers, of which he had a few, such as Guardiola, Carlo Ancelotti, Rafa Benitez, Jose Mourinho. 'It's not copy and paste,' he says. 'Never.' But he has that 'knowledge' and especially in regard to 'man-management' because he can recall how he felt when, say, Benitez wanted Liverpool to replace him with Gareth Barry in 2008.

Per sources, Chelsea's sporting leadership team, led by co-owner Behdad Eghbali and sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart, have loved working with Alonso thus far. They have seen his enthusiasm, and Alonso adds: 'I had a view of Chelsea from the outside. I could see the positives, and my concerns, so I addressed them. We are taking steps together, decisions to have a good team. This is the ultimate goal.'

Chelsea are also giving Alonso what he feels he needs to succeed, including bringing in Austin MacPhee as a set-piece specialist from Aston Villa. While not yet announced, he may fly to Hong Kong to team up with his new club there.

As for Chelsea's players, they have loved seeing how involved Alonso is in training. He sets them up for goals, for crosses, for passes - at the heart of each and every drill.

'When I am 10 years older, maybe I won't be able to do that, so I will be more on the sidelines,' says Alonso, who wears old-school Adidas Predators in sessions. 'But while I still can, I will enjoy it. I like to feel it. I like to be close to the players. That energy, it goes both ways. It is for them and for me.'

Alonso's training methods have already proved a hit among his squad who have 'big potential'

While Alonso is a good cook - his speciality is a Basque dish named Kokotxas - he will happily take good tapas restaurant recommendations in London if you have them. We did tell him about a place in Sydney called Deux Freres where he could take his staff after we tried it ourselves the night before. But living in the capital of England was a big draw for him and his family.

'It is not a case of going anywhere I want… no, no, no,' he says. 'It makes sense in this stage of our lives to come to London. My wife loves it. My daughters are coming. My son is going to university.'

Alonso's father, Periko, was a football player and manager. 'Because of my upbringing, the road was not unknown for me,' he says. 'I had seen that at home. It was all work.

'Preparing the training for the next day. Preparing the team selection. That was in the kitchen and I was next to him. So I'm not saying it was meant to be, but I had to try it.

'In the last part of my career, when I moved to Germany (Bayern Munich between 2014 and 2017 with Guardiola as his manager), that was important for me to start thinking about how I would do things. I was very curious. I was in that moment of my career where I could go to his office, 'Pep. Why is this happening? What's going to be the game plan?'

'Maybe when I was 20, I didn't have that confidence, to go to the manager's office to ask those things. But at that moment, because of the trust, I needed to do that, I wanted to do that. I felt much more responsible for the team than in my earlier years as a player. I wanted to not just think about myself but think about my team-mates and about how we were going to play and about supporting the young players. Where you are at in your early 20s is not the same as where you are at in your early 30s. We have seen this in many cases, and this was it in my case.

'Later, I wanted to try it (coaching), but not straight to the top level, so I started in the (Real Madrid) Under 14s. It felt natural, not to rush.'

While Alonso did not intend on sprinting to the top, he is too fast to have not made it here, now in charge of a club which harbours ambitions of winning the Premier League with him at the helm.

Sports.title: Kai Havertz warns Arsenal must improve again to defend their Premier League title with rivals making big signings - as Gunners chase Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior
Sports.content:
Kai Havertz warns Arsenal must improve again to defend their Premier League title with rivals making big signings - as Gunners chase Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kai Havertz warned that Arsenal need to evolve to defend their Premier League title and avoid being left behind by rival clubs who have strengthened over the summer.

The title holders are still working to finalise a marquee signing, having brought in £34million winger Christos Tzolis.

Bruno Guimaraes is expected to have his medical on Monday, while Arsenal are chasing Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior whose contract expires next summer.

Though the other 'Big Six' clubs have already invested heavily, which Havertz is acutely aware of.

He said: ‘I think we can and have to go further. You see other teams getting better so we have to step up another level again.

‘That’s what we are all here for, that’s what we train for, play those test (pre-season) games and reach our goals this season again.’

Kai Havertz believes Arsenal must improve again if they are to retain their Premier League title

The Gunners lifted the Premier League in May but have seen their rivals spend heavily this summer

Bruno Guimaraes is expected to have his medical on Monday, while Arsenal are chasing Real Madrid ’s Vinicius Junior

The taste of major silverware from last season has also left Havertz wanting to make up for lost time having previously finished as league runners-up for three consecutive seasons.

‘I think we want all the trophies,’ he added.

‘That's what we're here for. We missed out on a lot the last couple of seasons. Obviously, we won the Premier League now, but there's a lot more that we can do.

‘We have to reach another level to make that happen. We know how long the season is, we know how hard it is to go through the competitions. We want to do better again this year and make things happen again.’

Sports.title: Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts
Sports.content:
There are a number of pulls when it comes to a career in sport.

The chance to spend every day doing what you love, earning your living along the way. Or maybe the pursuit of glory, the drive to be the best at what you have dedicated your life to. How about the sometimes staggering prize money on offer, which can lead to the chance of fame and a lifestyle most can only dream of?

Few consider that, for some, it's not really a choice. It's what athletes know – what they have always done, so they will continue to do.

That seems to be the case for three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen, who this week spoke about how he's not a fan of darts and doesn't actually follow his sport.

And he's not alone. Some of the top names in tennis, football and more have expressed their dislike and distaste for the games that have given them so much.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at some of the world's top athletes who aren't actually too fond of the sport they have found success in.

Three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen revealed this week that he does not enjoy watching darts

Michael van Gerwen – Darts

Three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen has dropped down to world No 7 after the Matchplay, and his stocks have fallen significantly since his last world title in 2019.

The Dutchman has been speaking about his relationship with darts – the sport in which, perhaps for the first time in a decade, he is no longer the biggest star.

'I never did in my life,' he told Winmau of watching games. 'I don't even like watching darts.'

Luke v Luke (Littler and Humphries) has been the talk of the town for the last couple of years, while Littler has taken his game to a new dimension in recent months in becoming the first darts player to pick up £3million worth of earnings in two years.

Van Gerwen does make an effort to keep tabs on his rivals, but don't expect to see him in the crowd of any events he's not involved in any time soon, or listening to the likes of Wayne Mardle or Dan Dawson analysing the game on the tele.

But he doesn't totally hate the game. Just prefers to play it – which is fair enough, all things considered.

'Sometimes if a friend like Vincent (Van der Voort) used to play or things like that, or if Luke against Luke are playing maybe a final,' Van Gerwen continued on his viewing habits. 'I put on some live scores, but I'm not going to watch it at all.

'I'd rather play than watch. Simple as that. I always say the same, so it would be really weird to change my opinion.'

Ben White – Football

Arsenal defender Ben White has proven to be a bit of a diverse character in football in recent years. It all came to a head in November 2022, when he fell out with England assistant manager Steve Holland – supposedly over his attitude towards the game.

White is not a fan of watching football unless it's to analyse his own performances. Reports also emerged three years ago that White was not watching other analytical videos while with England.

'I watch myself for analytical reasons,' White recently claimed to The Overlap. 'I watch England, maybe, but I'm always busy doing something. I wouldn't just sit down and watch a game.

'I didn't ever watch football when I was younger. I still don't now.'

But, as is the case with Van Gerwen, it's not all hate with White. He just wants to be out there playing.

'I just loved the game,' he continued. 'I was always playing it, never watching.

'So I don't know too much about the older generations, but I know (Patrick) Vieira was a very good player. But I don't know the details.'

Ben White (right) has become known for his dislike of watching football

Serena Williams – Tennis

Serena Williams is perhaps the most famous name in women's tennis history, and one of the most dominant too.

'I don't love tennis today, but I'm here, and I can't live without it,' she told TennisNow in 2012. 'So I'm still here and I don't want to go anywhere any time soon.'

That's despite winning seven Australian Opens, seven Wimbledon titles, six US Opens and three French Opens. But it's not just tennis – it's sport on the whole.

'It's not that I've fallen out of love, I've actually never liked sports, and I never understood how I became an athlete,' she continued. 'I don't like working out, I don't like anything that has to do with working physically.'

Not too much of an issue, though, it seems...

Serena Williams revealed in 2012 that she doesn't love tennis - or sport on the whole

Nick Kyrgios – Tennis

Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios has had a bit of a love-hate relationship with his sport.

The Australian, who is planning retirement at the age of 31, reached his first Grand Slam final in 2022 at Wimbledon. He would lose to Novak Djokovic, but has also regularly made headlines for his actions away from the actual tennis, such as his shouting during matches.

One wonders if his relationship with tennis is related to that. He said in 2015: 'I don't really like the sport of tennis that much. I don't love it.'

He does, though, have love for a different sport.

'It was crazy when I was 14,' he continued. 'I was all for basketball and I made the decision to play tennis. I got pushed by my parents and to this day I can still say I don't love the sport. It is just crazy how things go.

'It's good when you're out there on a tennis court. There's nowhere to hide. It's all you, tactically, physically, mentally. But I just love basketball, I love the sport. I always have. I try when I'm on the road with tennis not to watch too many basketball videos and stuff like that, to keep me focused, but it's tough.'

What could have been.

Nick Kygrios has a love-hate relationship with the sport - and would rather have been a basketball player

Mark Williams – Snooker

Things seem to be going a little better for Mark Williams since his comments in 2019, when he became one of the few athletes to actively say they 'hate' their sport.

Currently World No 8 and a 2025 World Championship finalist, the Welshman was going through a tough patch back in 2019 when he had just beaten Fraser Patrick 6-2 in the first round of the UK Snooker Championship.

Despite actually being ranked No 3 in the world, Williams had failed to win a ranking event all year. He lashed out at snooker, and, like Kyrgios, his mind was elsewhere.

'I really struggled but somehow he struggled more than me and made it easy for me on a couple of frames,' Williams said. 'It's going all right, I'm enjoying myself when I'm on the golf course.'

When questioned on snooker, he added: 'Hate it. I'm just enjoying playing golf more.'

He had also talked about retirement in 2017, before going on to become world champion for a third time a year later.

Maybe he feels differently now.

Mark Williams admitted to 'hating' snooker in 2019 after teasing retirement a few years earlier

Tyson Fury – Boxing

Potentially the biggest name in modern boxing doesn't actually like boxing.

Tyson Fury has retired and un-retired countless times, but attributes his many returns to an addiction that helps him deal with his mental health struggles.

'I've tried to walk away many times and been unsuccessful,' he told DAZN in 2024. 'I meant it when I retired after Dillian Whyte back in 2022, I really meant that wholeheartedly. I could have put my hand on the Bible and meant it, but it was difficult to let it go.

'I've been in love with boxing from a little boy. It's been a love-hate relationship. When it's good, it's very good and when it's bad, it's very toxic. Now I am a fully grown adult with a family of my own.

'I wanted to walk away a lot of times but it always drags me back. Boxing is an addiction. It abuses my body, my mind, my soul. But I feel like it takes me to ecstasy. The rush is unbelievable. It gives me the biggest highs ever, but it also gives me the lowest lows. Boxing is more addictive than any drug ever. Ever. You can't let it go.'

It only takes a quick viewing of his reality show to see how much his family have begged him to pack it in. It seems, though, their words aren't enough.

Fury is set to take on Anthony Joshua in an all-British mega-fight later this year, having eased past Mariusz Wach last weekend. After that, he may well retire again – but will seemingly always keep on coming back.

Tyson Fury has tried to retire from boxing a number of times but finds himself returning

Benoit Assou-Ekotto – Football

A pattern emerges in the list of players who don't like their sport. They engage with it in some form all the time – every decision is based on their career, they have to analyse everything about it, and they spend most of their time performing it.

'I play it enough, don't I?' former Tottenham full back Benoit Assou-Ekotto once argued in an interview with Sky Sports.

'I don't watch football. I don't talk about football away from the game either. I suppose that is unusual. My interests are my friends and music, especially hip-hop. I like Ice Cube and 50 Cent.'

Assou-Ekotto played more than 200 times for Spurs, and didn't do too much wrong. Perhaps his argument proves you don't have to be totally obsessed with what you are doing to reach the top level – or maybe it suggests he could have gone higher if he was.

Former Tottenham defender Benoit Assou-Ekotto (right) is another sports star who does not enjoy watching their sport

Andre Agassi wrote in his autobiography that he 'hates' tennis despite his widespread success

Andre Agassi – Tennis

We have saved the most brutal for last – eight-time Grand Slam tennis champion Andre Agassi hates tennis.

'I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis,' he wrote in his autobiography. 'I hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.'

Tell us what you really think, Andre.

The American lashed out at the sport in his autobiography, explaining he was forced into it by his father and suffered some painful injuries. Players are also on tour for more than 30 weeks a year, have tennis dominate their lives, and undergo extreme stress.

Agassi won all there was to win. Others on this list have too. Still – it is not always enough. Showing that, sometimes, being a sports star may not be all it can seem to be.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal hit by fresh 'cheating' claims as umpire releases footage of ANOTHER player seemingly clicking fingers
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A fresh controversy has engulfed the amateur cricket club at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal after an umpire released footage appearing to show another player deploying the same tactic.

Saltburn Cricket Club has been at the centre of a storm after fielder Brian Devine allegedly cheated during a Second XI Division Two match against Norton. Video footage of Devine appearing to be clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of a bat edge, tricking the umpire into giving the batsman out, went viral on social media.

On Monday, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into Devine, 38, who has since been suspended by the club for the 'foreseeable future'.

Now, fresh footage has emerged appearing to show another Saltburn player successfully using the same tactic during a Third XI match against Marton.

The fielder appears to click his fingers as the ball flies past the bat and into the wicketkeeper's gloves, prompting the on-field umpire to give the batsman out. The footage was posted on social media by Berkshire-based umpire Andy Smy.

The captain of another team in the same league earlier this week claimed the alleged tactic had not been confined to Saltburn's victory over Norton.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

He said: 'It was not confined to just one game. I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out caught behind, but all of them said they hadn't touched the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to speak to him and threaten him with a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Earlier this week, Saltburn's Second XI forfeited their match against Marton, dumping themselves out of a cup competition, with a source close to the league saying 'none of the players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus'.

They did, however, return to the field on Saturday for a league match against Marton, where table-toppers Saltburn crashed to a nine-wicket defeat. With Devine no longer fielding at slip, Marton chased down their target of 101 in just 20 overs.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his alleged actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera seeming to be clicking his fingers

And Devine, a father and auction mart worker from Guisborough, North Yorkshire, is planning to 'lie low' until the scandal dies down.

A friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world - in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK, of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction from around the world has knocked him sideways.'

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said it was treating the allegations of cheating 'with the utmost seriousness' and called for the 'rights of all parties' to be respected amid intense scrutiny on social media.

'We would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account. There are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any wellbeing support we can,' the league said.

'Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media, it is imperative that, now this process is under way, the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and the right to a fair hearing for any individual or entity concerned.

'Anything less risks prejudicing any formal action which may follow.'

Saltburn, in a statement on Wednesday, said: 'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club run entirely by volunteers.'

Sports.content:
Man Utd star claims club can win Premier League after mood change under Michael Carrick

Manchester United have not won the Premier League since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, but could finally end the drought in 2026/27

View Image Michael Carrick has his work cut out (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Leny Yoro believes that Manchester United can win with Premier League this season. That's despite the club's welk-documented struggles for form since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement 13 years ago.

‌



The legendary Scottish manager earned 13 top-flight titles before bringing the curtain down on a remarkable coaching career in 2013. And in the years since, United have been through seven permanent managers as they have struggled to bring glory back to Old Trafford.

‌



While the club has seen success in various cup competitions in the wake of Fergie's exit, no man has been able to restore Premier League glory. David Moyes scraped a Community Shield in his lacklustre one-year stint with United, while Louis van Gaal saw success in the FA Cup.

Jose Mourinho bolstered the Old Trafford silverware collection with a Europa League, an FA Cup and a League Cup across his two-year reign, while Erik ten Hag guided United to both a League Cup and FA Cup triumph during his tenure.

Notably, it was only Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim who departed the club empty-handed, leaving behind nothing more than a mixture of fond and forgettable memories from their respective stints in Greater Manchester.

And despite Amorim overseeing a humiliating 15th-place finish in 2024/25, Yoro remains convinced that the tide is turning, with the club setting its sights on ending a 13-year Premier League drought.

‌



When quizzed about the prospect of lifting the Premier League title in the upcoming campaign, he said: "We're Man United so we have to think like that. And I know we have the potential to do it, so we have to do it.

Sports.title: Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title

Liverpool will hope that Andoni Iraola will be able to steady the Reds following a disastrous second season under Arne Slot but former hero Phil Thompson believes a title tilt could be on the cards

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is set to oversee his first campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool hero Phil Thompson believes the Reds could be contenders for the Premier League title under Andoni Iraola - but only if they avoid major injuries. The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins this summer following the decision to sack Arne Slot.

‌



The Dutchman lifted the Premier League crown in his debut season at Anfield but the Merseysiders struggled to hit those heights last term. Liverpool slipped to fifth in the table, just about squeezing into the Champions League.

‌



Since then, they have lost legendary figures Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson, while Ibrahima Konate quit the club for Real Madrid. Liverpool have invested since then, sealing deals for Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, while they are chasing a big-money transfer for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola.

‌



Giving his verdict on his former side, Thompson believes that another push for the title could be on the cards should Iraola have his star players available throughout the whole season.

"Iraola will need all of his players fully fit, but if we have a fully fit squad, we have a chance of winning the league this year, without question," Thompson told the BBC. “The fans want to see a bit more aggression, but I could see, just from watching (pre-season) from the stands, the demands of the manager.

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

"Andoni wants the ball to go forward and that's what we want to see. Go forward, quicker, more precise."

‌



And while a lack of injuries might push Liverpool up the table, Thompson also believes that having vocal leaders in the dressing room might also be a useful asset under their new boss.

"When you have a difficult time — a difficult couple of games or something — you need some strong voices in there, and you just feel like there is only Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker who remain at the club," Thompson added.

"I know people go, 'Oh, Dominik Szoboszlai'. But he has only been there a couple of years. He has to step up and I think he will do.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Thompson has shared his thoughts on Liverpool ahead of the new season (Image: Getty Images)

"But there are others around the team who you look to who will have to step up, to lay down some player rules."

Liverpool have just three more pre-season friendlies to navigate against Leeds, Monaco and Como before they kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign. The Reds get themselves underway against Newcastle United away from home, before their first match at Anfield against Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut
Sports.content:
Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro endured a nightmare home debut for Inter Miami

View 2 Images Former Man Utd midfielder Casemiro had a debut to forget for Inter Miami. (Image: (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images))

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro had a home debut to forget new club Inter Miami. The Brazilian scored an own goal in the 34th minute as Inter Miami drew with the Columbus Crew.

‌



The 34 year-old played a wayward pass to the opposition, diverting the ball past his own keeper as he tried to make amends by intercepting a cross. His blunder drew the Columbus Crew level after Luis Suarez's opener in the 16th minute.

‌



Casemiro was visibly frustrated by his mistake, but Inter Miami regained the advantage before the break. Noah Allen found the net in the fifth minute of first-half added time to put the home side back in front.

‌



Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Brais Mendez scored in the 84th minute to ensure a share of the spoils with a late equaliser. Despite his blunder, Casemiro played the full 90 minutes for the second consecutive match.

His first start delivered a 1-0 victory over Montreal that was marred by a serious injury sustained by his new team-mate German Berterame.

‌



The former Real Madrid star departed Manchester United at the end of the campaign, when his contract expired. The Brazil international enjoyed an impressive final season with United but revealed his intentions to move on at the start of the year.

The experienced midfielder represented his country at the World Cup before his new club was announced following Brazil's last-16 elimination. Casemiro penned a one-year contract, with an option to prolong his stint until 2029.

View 2 Images Casemiro scored an own goal in Inter Miami's draw with Columbus Crew. (Image: (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images))

‌



Speaking earlier in the week, Casemiro disclosed he'd fantasised about lining up alongside MLS sensation Lionel Messi. The World Cup runner-up entered the fray from the substitutes' bench against Columbus to realise his former adversary's ambition.

"The amount of trouble Messi gave me. of course, I dreamed of playing with him," Casemiro said. "I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed the help of my teammates.

"I am very happy to be alongside him now and I want to continue winning titles with him. I want to enjoy being alongside him, help him and make him even greater. He is one of the gods of football, if not the God of football himself, and I want to help."

‌



Casemiro's switch has arrived with its own share of controversy, though. The MLS confirmed they were examining his transfer after Inter Miami struck an agreement with LA Galaxy for the rights to secure his signature.

"The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete," the MLS said.

"While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority [first rights] to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot

A source described the FIFA President as a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor

Donald Trump addresses his call to Infantino over Balogun

Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away.

‌



A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

‌



The FA and UEFA, European football's governing body, said that they had lost confidence in Infantino.

In a stinging statement, which the English FA said it supported, Uefa described the scheme as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal he [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through".

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

View 3 Images And it's goodbye from him: Sources suggest Infantino's days at FIFA are numbered (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



It added: "The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."

Former FA chief Mark Pallios was among those calling on Infantino to go. He said: "He should not survive.

"He has delivered these plans with a complete lack of transparency." England legend Peter Reid slammed Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final.

"FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots."

CONCACAF, which governs the north and central American associations, plus the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Infantino's presidency.

‌



View 3 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during the 2026 World Cup draw (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident," CONCACAF said in a statement. "It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

‌



Uefa led the way in opposing the plan with its 55 members, including the FA, agreeing on Thursday to boycott all Fifa competitions.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," it said.

"We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story.

‌



"The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun."

Sources told the Sunday Times that senior figures in FIFA were looking to find a successor to Infantino.

View 3 Images Peter Reid the England legend called for Infantino to resign (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



A spokeswoman for the FA said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Infantino is likely to face an emergency FIFA council meeting where he will be asked to resign.

If he refuses, a single candidate backed by all his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year's election.

Article continues below

Candidates for the role include Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football president Sheikh Salman and Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al Khelaifi.

There may also be support for a less high-profile candidate who has backing from across the various continents.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow

The world record holder relaxed after he won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze

View 3 Images Josh Kerr with his Commonwealth Gold one mile medal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr joked that 'pressure is for tyres' today as he celebrated a turbo-charged Commonwealth gold in front of his home crowd in Glasgow.

‌



The world record holder won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze. The field also included fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished fifth.

‌



Kerr, 28, explained that he trained in the stadium as a teenager, learning how to 'win and lose'. Kerr joked that he did not feel the pressure after his world record mile two weeks ago adding: "Pressure is for tyres."

‌



View 3 Images Josh Kerr wins Commonwealth Gold in front of his home crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

On being named as 'King of Scotland,' he added: "Stop it. It was incredible, the fans packed the stadium and I knew that I had to seize the moment. I learned my craft there in Scotstoun stadium, it is where I learned how to win and lose. Winning in front of the home crowd was just incredibly special."

He thanked his childhood coach and said: "I am very, very proud to be an Eric Fisher athlete." Kerr said that he hoped to set an example for young athletes. Eric, who is still coaching in Glasgow, said he was very proud to guide both Kerr and Wightman when they were teenagers.

‌



A raucous home crowd roared with delight as Kerr took the lead in the final lap and crossed the finish line comfortably ahead of his rivals. The First Minister presented the athletes with their medals at a ceremony later in the evening.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr after his Commonwealth Gold (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Mr Swinney described Scotland’s performance in the Games as “truly historic and inspiring”. He said: “We’ve enjoyed some truly historic performances from Team Scotland at the Commonwealth Games – in swimming, bowls, athletics to name a few.

‌



“I hope that the Glasgow Games will encourage future generations to continue and build on this legacy of sporting greatness.”

The 11-day sporting extravaganza will end with tonight's closing ceremony at the Ovo Hydro. The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games has saved the British taxpayer around £600m - and may have secured the future of the event.

The total public funding allocated to stage the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games was £778 million. Birmingham City Council and local partners contributed £184m (25%) of that total.

Article continues below

The remaining 75% (£594m) was covered by the UK central government. Organisers of Glasgow 2026 say that using hotels instead of a village, along with smaller arenas and fewer events, cut costs to around £160m. Victoria in Australia was due to host the event and paid £199m to pull out which has funded Glasgow 2026 without taxpayers paying a penny.

Phil Batty, the chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: “This definitely isn’t the last hurrah for the Commonwealth Games. What we’ve seen is a wholesale shift in what the Commonwealth Games needs to do to sustain itself, not just through 2030, but through 2034, 2038 and beyond."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go

Gianni Infantino has been told to leave FIFA following the doomed plan to sell off the World Cup with UEFA and CONCACAF declaring losses of confidence in the current president

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has u-turned on the plan to sell a share in the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has been told to RESIGN from FIFA by a whopping 99% of Mirror readers. The president finds himself under huge pressure, having performed a dramatic u-turn on his plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to an investment group.

‌



FIFA announced the plot earlier this week, to widespread criticism from fans, governing bodies and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. There were suggestions that some confederations would consider boycotting any FIFA-organised competitions in the face of the plan.

‌



But Infantino and FIFA performed a huge backtrack by cancelling the proposal in its entirety. That, however, has not seen the current president escape criticism, with some still calling for the 56-year-old to be removed from his position.

‌



Since the baffling plan was originally unveiled, Mirror Football has been running a poll for fans to decide whether Infantino should resign or not. In total, 6832 fans had their say, with a huge 99 percent of them suggesting that Infantino’s position was now untenable.

That vote follows UEFA declaring a loss of confidence in the current president. A statement from UEFA on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA.

“You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been told to leave his post (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

CONCACAF followed suit with their own scathing statement, while bizarrely the Qatari FA have spoken out in support of Infantino.

A statement read: “We welcome FIFA President Gianni Infantino's decision to withdraw the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal in the interest of the global football community.

Article continues below

“While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among Member Associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
