World.title: 'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A press conference by Independent MP Pappu Yadav was disrupted in Delhi on Sunday after a confrontation broke out between his supporters and a group of men. Yadavâs media convenor alleged the MP was targeted with a knife in what he described as an attempt to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident.The incident occurred while Yadav was seated and speaking to the media. According to his media convenor, three or four men suddenly approached the MP and an altercation broke out. He alleged that one of the men first removed a slipper and hurled it before another attacker pulled out a knife."The attackers first took off a slipper and hurled it. When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result," the convenor said.He alleged he was beaten so badly by two or three individuals that he lost consciousness. "My associates carried me away from the spot. I have no further information," he said.A supporter of Yadav who was present said he instinctively put his hand in front of the MP as the knife was swung, causing the blade to graze his finger.The situation descended into a melee, with people falling and piling on top of one another.The convenor also alleged that Delhi Police personnel present did not intervene to protect Yadav and instead focused on taking the alleged attackers away. "I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The police seemed to be shielding the goons... Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. We don't know where they took them," he alleged."These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two' â they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," the convenor said, referring to the 2023 killing of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed and his brother in Prayagraj while they were in police custody.The convenor said he had met the DCP earlier in the day and submitted a formal complaint warning that the MP was arriving and had been receiving constant threats on social media. "Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here, and even they were merely protecting the goons," he alleged.He further alleged that several people had been positioned behind the media cameras before the incident. "There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper... The MP was the target, no one else," he said.According to people present at the scene, the confrontation began after some men allegedly accused Yadav of insulting Sanatan Dharma. The men argued with him before one of them removed a slipper and attempted to throw it. Yadav's supporters then intervened, leading to a scuffle.Yadav and his supporters have alleged the men were carrying knives and had intentions to kill him. The Delhi Police have not yet issued an official statement on the incident.Yadav himself alleged in a later statementthat the confrontation was an attempt on his life and linked it to threats against his family.âI came here because last night, they went to my childrenâs home. Now, you are trying to intimidate my children too; that wonât happen,â Yadav said. âI was with the press, and a conversation was underway. Amid that, there was an attempt to kill me.âHe alleged that some of those involved were calling for him to be killed, adding, âSome âBabaâ was saying, âBurn him alive,â while others were saying, âKill him.â If people hadnât been here, I would have been finished.âYadav also connected the confrontation to the ongoing controversy over alleged discrepancies involving offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.âI havenât said anything. I only asked Champat Rai or Giri Ji, where did the 200 kg of silver go? Where did the gold go?â he said.On security concerns, Yadav said he had repeatedly sought protection. âThe Delhi Police is quite capable. I have been demanding security for a long time now. What crime have I committed?â he said.The confrontation comes days after Yadav was involved in a political controversy over a protest by opposition MPs concerning alleged theft of offerings made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Yadav, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad and other opposition parliamentarians staged a demonstration in Parliament premises in which they enacted a skit depicting the alleged theft of temple offerings.Yadav wore saffron during the protest and portrayed a temple priest who allegedly took offerings from a donation box. The demonstration drew criticism from seers and others, who accused the MPs of insulting Sanatan Dharma.

World.title: Assam floods: 82 dead, 1.78 lakh affected as relief efforts intensify - key points
World.content:
Assam continued to grapple with the aftermath of devastating floods on Sunday, with the death toll remaining at 82 and nearly 1.78 lakh people still affected across seven districts.

Although floodwaters have begun to recede in some areas, thousands remain displaced, agricultural land is submerged, and the state government has intensified relief, rehabilitation and long-term mitigation efforts.

According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation has improved slightly, with the number of affected people declining from over 1.92 lakh to 1.78 lakh. However, 349 villages across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Bajali, Dhemaji and Sonitpur districts remain affected.

Charaideo is the worst-hit district, with more than 75,000 people affected, followed by over 58,000 in Sivasagar. Nearly 15,060 hectares of crop area remain submerged, while thousands of livestock have been affected or washed away.

Relief and rescue under way

A total of 44 relief camps are currently sheltering around 15,000 displaced people, while another 17 relief distribution centres are providing assistance to more than 5,500 residents.





The state government has directed district administrations to expedite the identification of affected families so that financial assistance can begin from August 3.

Villagers rescue over 1,000 people in Sivasagar

One of the most remarkable rescue stories emerged from the Nepali Khuti area in Sivasagar district, where local villagers used six country-made boats to rescue more than 1,000 people from five villages after floodwaters rose rapidly on July 19.

Residents said families were trapped on rooftops, elevated platforms and trees as water levels surged.

The volunteer rescuers continued operations through the night despite having little food or water, ferrying stranded villagers to safer areas.

CM reviews flood-hit districts and compensation plans

Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma began a tour of the worst-hit districts on Sunday to oversee relief operations and prepare for a comprehensive damage assessment exercise scheduled to begin on August 9.

The government has also directed officials to ensure uninterrupted distribution of relief kits, assess damage to educational institutions before schools reopen on August 10, and prepare restoration plans for damaged Namghars (Vaishnavite prayer centres).

IIT-Guwahati to be engaged for Brahmaputra erosion solution

During his visit to erosion-hit areas of Dibrugarh district, including Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria, Sarma announced that the state government will engage experts from IIT-Guwahati to develop a long-term solution to the Brahmaputra riverâs erosion problem.

Calling riverbank erosion one of Assamâs biggest geographical challenges, the chief minister said the state loses valuable land every year and that modern technology would be used to strengthen vulnerable riverbanks.

The proposed IIT initiative will complement the governmentâs planned Rs 90 crore erosion mitigation project.

Agriculture rehabilitation begins

Agriculture minister Pijush Hazarika visited Charaideo district on Sunday to review post-flood rehabilitation measures and launched community paddy nurseries and seedling distribution programmes for flood-affected farmers.

The government said quality seedlings and other assistance would be provided to ensure cultivation resumes without delay during the current agricultural season.

Aid pours in from NGOs, celebrities and political organisations

Support for flood-hit communities has continued to grow across Assam.

Actor Randeep Hooda joined a relief drive organised by Global Sikhs in Sivasagar district, distributing essential supplies and serving food through langar for affected families. He warned that prolonged waterlogging and mud-filled homes could trigger disease outbreaks and urged people across the country to contribute to relief efforts.

The Lok Janshakti Party (Ramvilas) has also launched a large-scale relief operation in Sivasagar, distributing food and essential supplies and announcing plans to feed up to 15,000 people daily for 10 days, along with setting up medical camps.

The Centre has approved Rs 379.35 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for Assamâs flood response. Sarma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for extending assistance and for deploying Inter-Ministerial Central Teams to support relief and rehabilitation planning.

Reliance Foundation has also contributed Rs 21 crore to the Chief Ministerâs Relief Fund for flood relief and rehabilitation efforts.

While water levels have started falling in parts of the state, the crisis is far from over. Thousands remain displaced, farmland continues to lie under water, and many families face the difficult task of rebuilding homes and livelihoods. Alongside immediate relief operations, the government is now focusing on compensation, agricultural recovery and long-term measures to address the recurring twin challenges of floods and Brahmaputra erosion.

World.title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
World.content:
Sheikh Hasina; Taslima Nasreen

Nasreen backs Uniform Civil Code , calls it necessary for women's equality

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday criticised the ban on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasinaâs Awami League party, calling it a "move against democracyâ and expressing uncertainty over Hasinaâs return to the country.âNo political party should be banned. The manner in which Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy. I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible,â Nasreen told reporters at a press conference in Kolkata.Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.Meanwhile, Nasreen alleged that several Awami League workers had been tortured and killed during Sheikh Hasinaâs exile and expressed uncertainty over whether the former prime minister would be able to return to Bangladesh.âMany Awami League workers were tortured and murdered. Sheikh Hasina wants to return, but I do not know whether that will be possible.But no one wants me to go back,â she said.Nasreen also criticised Jamaat-e-Islami, now Bangladesh's principal opposition party, accusing it of opposing womenâs equality and seeking the imposition of Sharia law.âNow we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an opposition party. It is against womenâs equality, and they want Sharia rule. If that happens, no minority will survive. Bangladesh is moving towards darkness. No one is trying to civilise Bangladesh. The government is only trying to remain in power,â she added.The 63-year-old author further claimed that âhatred against Hindusâ was being spread in some madrasas and mosques in Bangladesh.âIn many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus,â Nasreen remarked.Turning to the issue of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Nasreen said she had been advocating for such a law for the past 40 years and described it as essential in any âcivilised countryâ.âI have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country,â she remarked.She claimed that religious laws continued to affect womenâs rights in Bangladesh, alleging that Hindu women in the country lacked adequate legal protections, including the right to divorce.âIn Bangladesh, Hindu girls have no rights; they do not even have the right to divorce. Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more,â she alleged.In July, the BJP-led West Bengal government constituted a nine-member expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to examine and finalise a draft UCC for the state. The state government plans to introduce the legislation during the upcoming August Assembly session.Nasreen, who has lived in exile since 1994, when she was forced to leave Bangladesh due to the threat from Islamic radicals over her work, returned to Kolkata nearly two decades. She was forced to leave the city in 2007 following protests over her writings and memoir Dwikhandito (Split into Two), published in 2003.

World.title: Students from around the world experience the Jain way of life in Rajasthan
World.content:
Participants in the Jain Summer Program pose for a group photograph at Jain Vishwa Bharati in Ladnun, Rajasthan, on July 29. Photo by Aman Dhage/The American Bazaar

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(Aman

Dhage

contributed to the report.)

(By arrangement with

)

Nestled amid the arid plains of Rajasthan, about 230 miles west of Delhi, Ladnun is the kind of town many travelers might pass without a second glance. Its narrow streets, whitewashed temples, and unhurried pace stand in stark contrast to Indiaâs bustling metropolitan centers.This summer, however, the quiet town has become an unlikely destination for seekers of one of the worldâs oldest philosophies.For more than three centuries, Ladnun has been the spiritual home of the Terapanth order of Jainism, a reformist sect known for its disciplined monastic tradition and emphasis on nonviolence, self-restraint, and spiritual inquiry. Last month, those traditions welcomed an unusual group of visitors: nearly three dozen students, scholars, and faculty members from eight countries who are spending three weeks not merely studying Jainism, but living it.The immersive summer program, which began July 20 and concludes on Friday, is the result of a collaboration among Florida International University, California State University Long Beach, the Jain Education and Research Foundation (JERF), Jain Visva Bharati Institute, and southern California philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose support made the initiative possible.Rather than treating Jainism as an academic subject confined to classrooms and textbooks, the organizers designed a program that allows participants to experience the philosophy through daily practice.Each morning began with meditation. Students attended lectures on Jain philosophy, Prakrit â the ancient language of many Jain scriptures â and the foundational principles of âAhimsaâ (nonviolence), âAnekantavadaâ (the multiplicity of viewpoints), and âAparigrahaâ (non-attachment to possessions). They also interacted with monks and nuns, observed their disciplined routines, and experienced a lifestyle centered on simplicity, compassion, and mindfulness.âIt has been a very eventful week, and it has been a tremendous experience,â said Anne Vallely, a professor at the University of Ottawa and one of the foremost scholars of Jainism in the Western world.Describing the demanding schedule, she added, âWe have our lessons from 9:00 in the morning, and they go really into 10 oâclock, 11:00 at night.âThe program reflects months of planning by scholars in India and the United States.Florida International University, home to the first endowed chairs in Jain Studies in the United States, worked closely with California State University Long Beach, to develop the curriculum. The Jain Education and Research Foundation helped coordinate the academic and logistical aspects of the initiative, while Jain Visva Bharati opened its sprawling campus and monastic community to the international participants.At the heart of the effort is a broader mission: introducing Jain philosophy to a global audience at a time when its central teachings of nonviolence, environmental sustainability, restraint, and respect for diverse perspectives have taken on renewed relevance.Much of that vision has been championed by physician, entrepreneur, and philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose years of support for Jain education and higher learning have helped establish academic programs across the United States. Modi, who has contributed tens of millions of dollars to educational and religious causes in the United States, India, and globally, provided the principal financial support for this yearâs summer school.âI was born in India in the Jain faith, and those principles of Ahimsa, compassion, and respect for all living beings have guided my entire life as a physician,â the La CaÃ±ada, California,-based physician entrepreneur told The American Bazaar. ââ After my medical career, I realized philanthropy allows me to heal on a larger scale, not just one patient at a time. I contribute to Jain education because I believe Americaâs young students must be exposed to this ancient wisdom of tolerance, non-possessiveness, and plurality, which is so undervalued today. âThe program also coincided with another milestone.This year marks the 300th anniversary of the founding of the Terapanth order, giving participants an opportunity to witness commemorative events while learning about one of Jainismâs most influential traditions. Established in the 18th century by Acharya Bhikshu, the Terapanth order is distinguished by its centralized leadership and disciplined monastic structure. Its monks and nuns travel extensively to spread Jain teachings rather than remaining in permanent monasteries.Throughout the three weeks, students discovered that learning extended far beyond formal lectures.Meals became lessons in mindful eating. Silence became a form of reflection. Conversations with monks and nuns often continued long after scheduled sessions ended. Participants learned not only the philosophical foundations of Jainism but also how those principles shape everyday decisions, from food and consumption to conflict resolution and environmental responsibility.For many students, the immersive setting transformed abstract ideas into lived experience.âIâm surrounded by scholars and Iâve gotten to meet with sadhvis and sadhus, and itâs just been lovely,â said Carol Rodriguez, one of the participants, who holds a Ph.D. in Jain Studies from the University of Florida.The Cuban-born scholar earned her bachelorâs and masterâs degrees in Jain Studies from Florida International University in Miami, where she translated portions of the Lilavatisara, a 13th-century work by Jain monk Jinaratnasuri.The international composition of the group further enriched the discussions. Participants brought diverse academic backgrounds and cultural perspectives, creating conversations that reflected Jainismâs emphasis on dialogue and multiple viewpoints rather than absolute certainty.Organizers hope the program will serve as a model for future international collaborations in religious studies, philosophy, sustainability, and peace education.Unlike traditional study abroad programs, the Ladnun initiative invites participants to become temporary members of a living spiritual community, where learning occurs as much through observation and daily practice as through formal instruction.As the summer school concludes on July 7, participants will return to universities and communities around the world carrying more than lecture notes and academic credits. They will leave with firsthand experience of a philosophy that has quietly endured for millennia and memories of a small Rajasthan town where, for three weeks, Jainism was not simply studied, but lived.

World.title: Heavy silt inflow disrupts water supply in parts of Kannur
World.content:
Heavy silt inflow into the Pazhassi dam following intense rain and landslips in the catchment disrupted drinking water treatment, reducing water supply to parts of Kannur and adjoining areas on Sunday (August 2, 2026).

Kerala Water Authority (KWA) officials said the issue was not contamination but unusually high turbidity caused by excessive mud content in the raw water. They added that the water could be treated safely only after turbidity levels declined. At the Pazhassi water treatment plant, turbidity was measured at around 125 Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU), whereas efficient treatment is possible only when it falls below 50 NTU.

A senior KWA official said NTU measures the cloudiness, or turbidity, of water by indicating how suspended particles scatter light. Higher NTU values indicate muddier water, while lower values indicate clearer water. “The issue is not that the water cannot be treated. When turbidity is very high, the treatment capacity drops sharply and the filters clog quickly,” the official told The Hindu.

The official said water treatment was suspended after tests conducted on Saturday (August 1, 2026) night showed excessive turbidity. Engineers are monitoring water quality every hour, and pumping will resume once turbidity levels fall to safer limits, he added.

The Pazhassi treatment plant supplies around 30 million litres a day (MLD) of drinking water to Kannur town and surrounding areas, including Valapattanam and Chirakkal. The disruption has affected water supply in these areas.

According to KWA officials, the muddy water is the result of landslides and heavy runoff in the forested upper catchments, reportedly in Karnataka, that feed the Pazhassi dam. Continued rainfall could prolong the problem by keeping turbidity levels high.

Officials said the situation would improve if rainfall subsides and advised consumers to use stored water judiciously until normal pumping resumes. They added that the disruption was expected to ease once the raw water became clearer.

World.title: Cauvery water from Kabini to reach Tamil Nadu soon
World.content:
Water released from the Kabini Dam in Karnataka is expected to reach the Tamil Nadu boundary on Monday (August 3, 2026) and flow into the Mettur Dam by Monday night or Tuesday (August 4), according to Water Resources Department (WRD) officials.

Following heavy rainfall over the past few days in Karnataka, the Karnataka government began releasing Cauvery water from the Kabini Dam on Saturday (August 1). Officials had initially expected the water to reach Tamil Nadu by Sunday (August 2) evening. However, the flow has been delayed as the water is moving slowly through the dry Cauvery riverbed.

WRD officials at the Mettur Dam said water was first released from the Kabini Dam at 500 cusecs on Saturday (August 1) morning. The discharge was gradually increased to 5,000 cusecs in the afternoon before reaching 25,000 cusecs by Saturday night.

They said the dry riverbed had absorbed a significant amount of the released water, slowing its downstream movement. As a result, the water is now expected to reach the Mettur Dam on Monday (August 3) night or Tuesday.

“We expect the present discharge of 25,000 cusecs to continue for the next few days. If the Mettur Dam receives 25,000 cusecs of inflow for an entire day, the water level will rise by about four feet. Once the reservoir level crosses 90 feet, the government will decide on releasing water from the dam for delta irrigation,” WRD officials said.

Officials said Tamil Nadu is likely to receive a substantial quantity of Cauvery water only after the Krishnaraja Sagar (KRS) Dam fills up. The dam is yet to reach capacity. At present, the reservoir holds around 20 tmc ft of water against its storage capacity of 49.45 tmc ft.

“If the current spell of rain continues, the KRS Dam is expected to reach capacity within the next 10 days. Thereafter, surplus water from Karnataka is expected to flow into the Mettur Dam,” the officials added.

On Sunday (August 2), the water level at the Mettur Dam stood at 73.33 feet against its full reservoir level of 120 feet. The storage stood at 35.63 tmc ft, compared with the dam’s capacity of 93.47 tmc ft. Inflow into the reservoir increased to 47 cusecs from 42 cusecs, while the discharge for drinking water purposes into the Cauvery river was maintained at 1,500 cusecs.

World.title: Former BJP MP Rebati Tripura steps back from politics, returns to teaching
World.content:
Senior BJP leader and former Lok Sabha MP Rebati Tripura has returned to his teaching profession, taking a break from active politics. Mr. Tripura has joined Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Higher Secondary School in Agartala as a post-graduate teacher in the political science stream.

The indigenous leader, who was a critic of Tipra Motha Party founder and royal scion Pradyot Kishore Debbarman and the latter’s style of politics, did not find a senior position in the recently restructured State committee of the BJP. He was one of few tribal leaders who helped the saffron party grow organisation in hills and interior tribal communities.

Understanding with party

Mr. Tripura was not re-nominated in the East Tripura (ST) constituency in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections as BJP was desperate to keep the seat in its fold. The party nominated Kriti Devi Debbarman, who made her debut in politics as part of an understanding with the Tipra Motha Party founder.

She was elected mainly due to the backing of the Tipra Motha Party, which had already made a surge in the State’s tribal political arena. The Lok Sabha results also paved the regional party’s entry into the coalition government, but the party repeatedly gave crushing blows to the BJP in the tribal autonomous district council elections.

Mr. Tripura, who served as an MP from 2019 to 2024, continued his criticism of the Tipra Motha Party while senior leaders of the BJP have adopted a guarded criticism. He, however, did not publicly oppose the BJP for its alleged hobnobbing with Tipra Motha.

World.title: Karnataka Cabinet expansion most likely on August 3
World.content:
After days of deliberations and lobbying, the much-awaited Cabinet expansion is likely to take place on Monday evening with the Karnataka government learnt to have informally sought time from Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot for the swearing-in of new Ministers at Lok Bhavan.

While the list containing names of the legislators to be sworn in is expected to reach Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Monday morning from the Congress Central leadership, party sources said that many of the chosen legislators could be intimated soon after the list arrives.

Sources said that though the Central leadership had preferred Saturday for the swearing-in with the list being ready, it had been postponed for an ‘astrologically favourable day’, which happens to be Monday. “Informally, the government has sought time between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. on Monday from the Governor,” sources said.

On Sunday, when presspersons asked Mr. Shivakumar about the absence of the Governor in Bengaluru, he said that Mr. Gehlot will be returning on Monday.

Sources said that speculation about who would be lucky to enter the Cabinet has been doing the rounds, but the leaders have been tight-lipped over the names. “The lists carried by Mr. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah are believed to have undergone changes as the party is looking to bring in a balance.”

The party is walking a tightrope with over 50 legislators aspiring to be Ministers, and its decision has to take into account regional, caste and community equations. “One of the important criteria has been the winnable factor in the next elections and their influence in their region to help other party candidates win in the 2028 elections,” sources said.

Sources said that competition is intense among Muslim legislators from Bengaluru that has turned out to be a stress point with elections to five corporations in Greater Bengaluru Authority region expected to be held shortly. “Similarly, with the KPCC president post going to B.K. Hariprasad, an OBC, demand for a higher share for Lingayats has emerged and there are many competing forces within the community. Some senior legislators are also lobbying for the post of the Speaker.”

The list has been drawn considering the post of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council, sources added.

World.title: Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra shifts shows amid opposition from Hindutva outfits
World.content:
Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.

The development comes after a Hindutva outfit, Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samiti, petitioned the Whitefield police, demanding that Mr. Kamra should not be permitted to perform.

They had contended that Mr. Kamra had disrespected Hindu deities.

A senior police official from the Whitefield Division told The Hindu that Mr. Kamra and the organisers of the shows visited the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday and informed that they had decided to cancel the shows. The decision, they said, was taken as the event had become controversial. No law and order incident was reported in connection with the scheduled performance.

Taking to social media platform X, Mr. Kamra on Sunday announced: “Shows for Monday - Tuesday - Wednesday - Thursday shifted to Underground Comedy Club in Koramangala.”

He further said that amount would be refunded to those who had already booked tickets for the Whitefield shows and requested them to book shows at the Koramangala venue afresh.

On Saturday, responding to the Hindutva activists objecting to his shows in Whitefield, Mr. Kamra gave an open invite on X that he would be at the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday to seek permission to perform and any objectors were free to join him to debate on “comedy and culture”. He later said only senior journalist Aakar Patel turned up.

Meanwhile, Mohan Gowda, spokesperson, Hindu Janajagruti Samiti, said that Mr. Kamra shifted the shows after facing strong opposition and appealed to the Koramangala police not to allow him to perform in their jurisdiction.

Sources in the government said that the shows would be not stopped.

World.title: Day before bypoll result, Congress suspends ex-Datia MLA Rajendra Bharti
World.content:
A day before the result of the recently held by-election to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly seat, the Congress suspended former MLA Rajendra Bharti — whose disqualification necessitated the bypoll — from the party’s primary membership.

The suspension comes days after the Congress candidate for the bypoll, Ghanshyam Singh, accused Mr. Bharti of trying to sabotage his campaign and colluding with the Bharatiya Janata Party. Mr. Bharti, however, alleged that Mr. Singh had been colluding with senior BJP leader and former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra, who was denied the ticket by the ruling party.

“With the approval of the president of the All India Congress Committee (AICC), Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, Rajendra Bharti, former MLA from Datia, is hereby suspended from the primary membership of the Indian National Congress with immediate effect,” Harish Chaudhary, Congress general secretary in-charge of Madhya Pradesh, said in a statement.

Bypoll to the Datia Assembly seat was held on July 30 and the votes will be counted on August 3. The constituency recorded a voting turnout of 71.44%, as per the Election Commission.

The bypoll was necessitated following the disqualification of Mr. Bharti in April due to his conviction in a bank fraud case.

The BJP fielded debutant Ashutosh Tiwari, after snubbing former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra who represented the seat for three consecutive terms until his defeat to Mr. Bharti in the 2023 Assembly polls. The Congress fielded Mr. Singh, a member of the erstwhile Datia royal family and former MLA from neighbouring Sewda Assembly seat.

Towards the end of campaigning days in Datia, Mr. Bharti and Mr. Singh levelled allegations against each other, including about receiving funding from BJP leaders. Mr. Singh also accused Mr. Bharti of not supporting his campaign in the bypoll.

Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Bharti’s son Ankit Bharti said, “Ghanshyam Singh has been very close to Narottam Mishra for several years and has worked against Congress candidates in the past. Even for this election he has received funding from Narottam as he is also working against BJP because he did not get the ticket. But he [Mr. Singh] has alleged that my father has received funding from the BJP to support their candidate [Mr. Tiwari].”

Mr. Bharti and Mr. Mishra have been political rivals for more than a decade with the former ending the BJP leader’s three-term tenure as Datia MLA in the 2023 election.

A leader close to Mr. Bharti also said he “had a role” in the BJP’s decision to deny Mr. Mishra the ticket.

World.title: Bangladesh court grants bail to jailed Hindu rights leader; release from prison unlikely
World.content:
Bangladesh’s High Court on Sunday (August 2, 2026) granted bail to jailed Hindu rights leader Chinmoy Krishna Das in two cases, his lawyer said. But the bail would not ensure his immediate release from prison because he is accused in four other cases.

Mr. Das is a Hindu monk whose arrest in November 2024 on sedition charges for allegedly disrespecting the national flag sparked protests and communal tensions in Bangladesh. He was subsequently booked in several additional cases, including charges of murder, attempted murder and vandalism.

India back then expressed "deep concern" over the arrest and asked Dhaka to ensure the safety "of Hindus and all minorities".

It came at a time when India-Bangladesh relations turned frosty following the August 2024 ouster of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina — driven by her asylum in New Delhi and political friction with the interim government.

“The (two-judge) High Court bench granted his bail petition in two cases involving charges of murder attempts, vandalism and obstructing officials in performing their duties,” Mr. Das’s lawyer Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya said on Sunday.

Both prosecution and defence lawyers said the decision of the Bench would not ensure Mr. Das’s release because of four more pending cases, including charges of treason and murder, against him.

The murder case concerns an incident in which a government prosecutor was hacked to death in the southeastern port city of Chattogram by activists protesting Mr. Das’s arrest.

Mr. Das, who was previously associated with ISKCON, is a spokesman for a group named Hindu group Sammilito Sanatan Jagaran Jote. The group organised several rallies in Bangladesh, demanding minority rights, safety and protection from civil unrest in 2024 after the ouster of Hasina following a violent student-led street protest.

The cases against Mr. Das are in different stages in the courts.

His lawyers have sought bail for a while, saying Mr. Das was languishing in jail for a long time with ailments.

Several of his earlier bail petitions were either rejected or stayed.

World.title: Bengaluru’s civic woes
World.content:
Over the last month, residents of Bengaluru have witnessed the Karnataka government waking up to some age-old problems such as encroached footpaths, garbage blackspots, footpath riding and the like.

Spearheaded by the new Greater Bengaluru Development Minister, Krishna Byre Gowda, back-to-back drives since July 1 saw civic authorities attempt to reclaim the city’s notoriously bad pedestrian infrastructure from encroachments by commercial establishments, street vendors, abandoned vehicles, and garbage dumps — problems that most residents had simply resigned to live with.

Though citizens have welcomed the drives, street vendors argue that they were never given vending zones. Moreover, garbage dumping and blackspots exist mostly due to inefficient waste collection as well as civic apathy. In some cases, dumping is carried out by the civic workers themselves due to the lack of waste transfer stations.

The drive to clear footpaths in the city led to altercations between street vendors and civic authorities; in one such clearance drive in Shivajinagar, miscreants even attacked the officials carrying out the drive. Citizens also reported that several of the encroachments that were cleared were back to how they were days after the clearance drive.

The Minister maintained that the aim was not to displace anyone but to create safe pedestrian infrastructure at least on the arterial roads; he said that vendors could move to the inner roads to continue business. However, street vendor unions have questioned this logic, pointing to the lack of will by successive governments to streamline street vending by assigning ID cards and notifying vending zones, so as to prevent harassment from anti-social elements and enforcement agencies. Mr. Gowda later directed corporation officials to conduct a fresh survey of street vendors as the previous survey had enumerated only a little over 30,000 street vendors, while the actual number exceeds 80,000. He also instructed them to identify vending zones.

In the case of abandoned vehicles, the Minister clarified that the campaign is not aimed at vehicles in regular use, admitting that parking regulations requiring houses to have dedicated parking spaces had not been enforced for decades, resulting in residents having to park their vehicles on public roads.

Lack of planning

Urban planning experts and residents have repeatedly pointed to one lacuna when it comes to Bengaluru: the lack of a long-term vision that can keep pace with the level of growth the city experiences. This, they have argued, applies to many areas, from planning the Namma Metro network, that is yet to reach the Kempegowda International Airport, to ensuring connectivity to Bengaluru’s rapidly expanding boundaries.

To address what is easily the city’s best claim to infamy, its traffic, the Congress Government has pushed for new tunnel roads and flyovers. However, urban experts and citizens’ groups have continuously argued against them, reasoning that the city’s public transport should be strengthened instead of introducing short-term solutions for the growing number of private vehicles.

Another case in point is the city’s way of addressing its water needs. As Bengaluru’s once famed network of lakes has been undermined by infrastructure projects, the government is focussed on bringing solutions from afar. Every drought-hit year threatens the Cauvery dependent-city’s water security.

The State government, under the leadership of the new Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, is pushing aggressively for the positioning of Bengaluru as a prime investment destination. As Bengaluru continues to function without an elected civic council since 2020, with the State government facing pressure from the Supreme Court to conduct elections this year, the emphasis on mega projects such as tunnel roads is being seen as an attempt to tilt the odds towards the Congress.

But since there is no assurance on when these big-ticket projects would be realised, the slew of new drives to fix basic pedestrian problems are the ones that could provide instant relief to citizens. There is a growing call for the government to improve the quality of life of the citizens by first fixing the basics before moving on to big-ticket projects.

World.title: At least 14 people, including police officials, martyred in suicide attack on Kabal police station in Swat: police
World.content:
At least 14 people, including police officials, were martyred and at least 18 others injured in a suicide attack on Swat’s Kabal police station on Sunday, police and rescue officials said.

Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, while speaking to Dawn, confirmed the death toll.

Malakand Division Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain told AFP that police officers were among those martyred.

He added that another body, suspected to be that of the bomber, had been brought to the hospital.

According to the Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Umar Khan, the suicide bomber detonated explosives after police personnel attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station.

The DPO said that the police remained on high alert. “Security forces have cordoned off the area, and an investigation is underway to collect further evidence,“ he added.

The explosion occurred near the gate of Kabal police station while hundreds of people were participating in a public demonstration at nearby Kabal Chowk against the recent wave of terrorism in Swat Valley.

Police officials inspect the site following a suicide bombing during a protest in Swat district on August 2. — AFP

The bodies of nine victims were shifted to Central Hospital Saidu Sharif, while the bodies of five others were moved to Kabal Hospital, where doctors confirmed their deaths, said Rescue 1122 Spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi.

The spokesperson added that two of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.

The powerful blast caused multiple casualties, prompting an immediate emergency response from police, rescue teams and local authorities. Security personnel also sealed off the area and launched a search operation.

The protest had drawn a large crowd from across the district and the attack occurred as the final speaker was addressing the crowd, triggering panic among participants. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Addressing the gathering before the blast, the speakers condemned the resurgence of terrorism in Swat and demanded that the government ensure lasting peace. They said their movement had a single agenda: the restoration of peace and the elimination of terrorism from the region.

The speakers stressed that maintaining law and order and eradicating terrorism were the state’s responsibility, warning that continued insecurity could trigger widespread public unrest, citing recent protest movements in other countries as examples of growing public frustration.

The speakers also criticised the authorities for what they described as action against peaceful citizens while terrorists continued to operate in the mountainous areas of Swat. They alleged that terrorists had openly circulated videos on social media and questioned why stronger action had not been taken against them.

“Our children deserve education, and our families deserve to live in peace,” one speaker told the gathering.

“We have witnessed years of bloodshed. Our mothers, sisters, and daughters have suffered immensely, and we do not want another generation of widows and orphans.”

Condemnations pour in

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the loss of life and called for a comprehensive investigation into the incident, according to a statement issued by his office on X.

President Zardari directed the relevant authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to those injured.

“Terrorists will never succeed in their nefarious efforts to undermine peace, national unity and the writ of the state,” he was quoted as saying. He added that the sacrifices of the KP police were “a source of pride for the entire nation”.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast.

“Terrorists cannot demoralise the nation with cowardly attacks,” Kundi was quoted as saying, as per a statement.

KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, condemning the incident, sought a report from the KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) and offered condolences to the families of the deceased.

“The elements hostile to peace will never be allowed to succeed in their nefarious intentions,” the chief minister was quoted as saying.

Earlier in the day, an IED blast near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza injured two policemen in the provincial capital Peshawar. On July 30, a terrorist attack on a police checkpost in Hangu martyred nine policemen.

KP has seen an uptick in terrorist activity. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’s monthly security assessment, KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 terrorism related deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105 per cent.

World.title: Second phase of AJK polls concludes amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
World.content:
The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies.

Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension.

The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported.

Polling in LA-27, commonly known as Kutla, was deferred until August 4 after polling material could not be dispatched due to a landslide.

Similarly, polling in 52 of the 147 polling stations of LA-28 (Muzaffarabad-II) was also postponed until August 4 for the same reason.

Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions.

What has happened so far:

Polling postponed in LA-27 due to rain; 4 other seats up for grabs in Muzaffarabad district, 2 each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley

Voting held across country for 12 refugee seats — 7 in Punjab, other 5 divided between different provinces

Bilawal condemns ‘attack’ on party’s regional president, says PPP worker killed in LA-31

PML-N disputes PPP claim, says man died from heart failure

PPP alleges electoral malpractices at some polling stations in at least 11 constituencies

Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well.

In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on the party’s regional president, Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V).

Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency.

“The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged.

The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately.

In a separate statement, Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).”

He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”.

The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar.

The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals.

It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident.

AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice.

The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”.

Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death.

He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations.

In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building.

Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far.

Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division.

Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital.

Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services.

He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details.

“We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said to a question.

Preliminary, unofficial results

According to preliminary and unofficial results, the PML-N was leading in seven constituencies, while the PPP was ahead in three as vote counting continued in the second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) local elections.

The PML-N was leading in LA-25 by 1,364 votes, LA-29 by 379 votes, LA-30 by 247 votes, LA-31 by 2,934 votes, LA-32 by 892 votes, LA-35 (Jammu-II) by 18,788 votes and LA-36 (Jammu-III) by 10,002 votes.

Meanwhile, the PPP was ahead in LA-26 by 1,745 votes, LA-28 by 1,782 votes and LA-33 by 1,349 votes.

In constituencies where the PML-N was leading, the PPP was running second except in LA-35, where an independent candidate was in second place. Where the PPP was ahead, the PML-N was in second position, according to preliminary and unofficial results.

Info ministry criticises foreign media coverage

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections, accusing the channel of “selective reporting” from “handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad.

In a post on X, the ministry alleged that the channel had sought to “misrepresent” the elections and voting process through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”.

It alleged that it was aimed at “delegitimising” the electoral exercise and undermining the will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK.

PML-N says man did not die from bullet, had heart failure

On its part, the PML-N disputed the PPP’s stance on a man’s death in Muzaffarabad, saying that he died due to heart failure and did not suffer any bullet injury.

Responding to the PPP’s stream of allegations in a media talk in Rawalpindi, PML-N Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb said a man aged between 68 and 70 years was trying to resolve a “scuffle” when he suffered heart failure.

She noted that there was a physical altercation between groups of the PML-N and the PPP, describing the incident as “unfortunate”. She further said that Shah’s family has refused to have a post-mortem examination conducted.

“Will you do politics on bullets? Will you sabotage a democratic process by spreading such fake claims?” Aurangzeb said.

She further said, “My brothers, this politics of bullet, this politics of robbing votes, this does not suit parties like us.”

The PML-N leader went on to emphasise that the PPP leadership had given sacrifices and spent their “entire lives” in making efforts to strengthen democracy.

She remarked that ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto “did not give sacrifice to see this day”.

“You should remember that you are Zulfikar Ali Bhutto’s grandson. We will keep reminding you because we will not let their sacrifices go to waste.”

She further said that the PPP was aware that the public did not vote for it. “Are elections won by crying, grabbing collars, issuing threats or making accusations? Elections are won with courage.”

The PML-N leader also took exception to Bilawal’s remarks of “snatching away seats” and “taking out seats”, saying: “Bilawal, you say good things. What kind of statements are you making now?”

Aurangzeb compared the PPP’s attitude to that of the PTI, saying the former’s “narrative” should not be the same.

“Find out so that you may not have to cry in Sindh,” the PML-N leader cautioned the PPP, noting people in Sindh were seeking performance similar to that of the Punjab government.

Aurangzeb recalled the Charter of Democracy signed between the PPP and the PML-N in 2007, stressing that its purpose was not to let democratic processes be sabotaged.

Noting that the PPP was in power in AJK and had its administrative machinery in the region, the PML-N leader questioned if Bilawal’s “own government is carrying out rigging against you”.

She remarked that if one considered the PPP’s allegations to be true, the party would have to “accept” that its own government “carried out rigging against Bilawal”.

Aurangzeb said the PPP-led administration was preventing the transportation of the required electoral equipment.

She also commented on Bokhari showing ballot papers stamped with votes for PML-N, saying, “This is an election of thousands of votes. He was showing two stamps on two ballot papers.”

The Punjab minister took aim at the PPP’s governance, saying that it had nothing to show for its performance. She quipped that voters were yet to head to polling stations early in the morning while the PPP had already started holding media talks on rigging.

Aurangzeb said that if the PPP still had reservations, there were relevant platforms such as the Election Commission and tribunals to approach, rather than hold press conferences.

“Contest the elections. Do not cry out loud,” she said.

In a similar tone, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also regretted the rigging allegations levelled by the PPP.

“Unfortunately, a democratic party, which is also a signatory to the Charter of Democracy, has been alleging rigging since 10:30 in the morning,” he said while addressing the media in Islamabad.

Flanked by Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam, Sanaullah claimed that the second phase of polls in AJK was conducted in a “peaceful manner”.

The inter-provincial coordination minister said the electoral process was completed at 96 per cent of polling stations, adding that vote counting was underway.

Sanaullah maintained that it was the “most transparent and non-violent electoral process”, adding that a few incidents had occurred during the day.

Referring to the alleged attack on PPP leader Akbar, Sanaullah said it was a dispute involving another family in the area and that there had been “no physical confrontation”, only a verbal argument.

Contesting the PPP’s claim about the second reported incident involving a party worker, the PML-N leader said a citizen named Mushtaq was involved in a scuffle with his family members, one of whom pushed him.

“He reportedly went home afterwards and then suffered a heart attack as he was a cardiac patient. They [PPP] claimed that shots were fired, but not a single bullet was fired,” the premier’s adviser asserted.

Sanaullah added that the PML-N condoled his death, but that the “deceased individual was not a PPP worker”.

PPP alleges electoral malpractices

On Sunday, the PPP alleged electoral malpractices shortly after polling commenced, with several of the complaints claiming its polling agents at some stations were not allowed to observe the voting process.

At 2pm, the party also wrote a separate letter to the Election Commission requesting follow-up on 25 complaints filed by it regarding 11 constituencies.

The PPP said it had not received any formal written response or acknowledgement from the electoral watchdog on the status of any of the 25 complaints.

“Given the gravity, number and geographical spread of the violations documented, the Party respectfully submits that a formal response from the Commission is now overdue and urgently required.”

On the other hand, the PML-N’s social media posts revolved around voters across Muzaffarabad and Punjab showing up to cast ballots with “enthusiasm”.

Several posts highlighted that a large number of voters were flocking to the PML-N’s election camps, rather than those of rival parties.

The PML-N also wrote to the Election Commission in response to a PPP complaint about LA-40 (Valley-I), terming the latter’s allegations against its candidate Muhammad Naeem Khan as “baseless”.

In the letter, seen by Dawn, the PML-N asserted that the allegations “regarding administrative failures are unsubstantiated and appear to be an attempt to create unnecessary controversy around the polling process”.

The PML-N urged the electoral watchdog to ensure that “no misleading or politically motivated complaint is allowed to undermine public confidence in the integrity of the polling”.

At a polling station in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI), the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station.

In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”.

In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station.

The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”.

The PPP also alleged a PML-N MPA at a polling station in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Abbottabad of obstructing the voting process for the refugee seat of LA-45 (Kashmir-VI).

In LA-25 (Neelum-I), the PPP said the voting process at a polling station had been halted after reports emerged of PML-N supporters tearing up ballot papers.

The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action.

‘Polling agents excluded’

The party alleged that its polling agents were not allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene.

The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34.

Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”.

It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”.

“The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged.

The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”.

Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil.

The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process.

Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI).

Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties.

At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters.

Other issues

In a separate statement in the morning, the party claimed that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling.

Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time.

Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzaffarabad.

The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure.

PML-N slams ‘blame game’

Earlier in the day, PML-N’s Muqam called on political parties not to indulge in a “blame game”.

“Nothing is to be gained from a blame game,” he said during a press conference in Islamabad, adding that law enforcement personnel were also deployed to ensure security.

“They should not act in a manner that ‘why was I not given seats’,” Muqam said, stressing that it was the public whose votes allocate seats.

The minister urged all political parties to let the electoral process take place in a peaceful manner, stressing that making allegations without evidence cannot change the results.

At the same time, Muqam also highlighted “arbitrary transfers and administrative decisions” in AJK, where the PPP is in power. He said the moves “seemed discriminatory”.

He recalled that the PML-N had accepted the results of elections in Gilgit-Baltistan held in June, where the PPP emerged the winner and formed the government.

Defending the results from Mirpur, Muqam asserted that the people voted for PML-N due to its performance.

On the other hand, PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan also held a press conference where he called on the Election Commission to play its role in “proving” the election process in AJK to be free and fair.

“Azad Kashmir is an international issue … people’s eyes are on it,” the former MNA said, adding that if the commission did not recognise the public and assure a free election, “tomorrow we will not be able to ratify this election under any circumstance”.

He recalled that after the Mirpur polls, there was a detailed discussion within the party about boycotting the second and third phases. However, the party leadership refused the idea of a boycott.

Chan cautioned that if the PPP was “compelled” to move towards such steps for the third phase, it would benefit those who wanted to prove the election “dirty”.

“I see this becoming an ultra Form-47 election,” he said.

He said that in negotiations in Muzaffarabad, the PPP had provided proof of rigging in four constituencies, as well as agreeing to hold re-polling in any other constituencies in which there were objections.

He also called for a benchmark for voting, saying, “General polling was less than 30 per cent. But wherever you won, it was 80pc, 90pc, 75pc … this doesn’t even happen in urban cities like Islamabad and Lahore.”

‘Admission of rigging’

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling.

Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polls in Mirpur, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday.

A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts.

Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, Bilawal said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored.

“The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.”

According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala.

Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed.

Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections.

A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N.

Election numbers

According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts.

Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu.

A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad and KP, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray.

In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections. The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat.

In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh.

In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh.

In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh.

For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan.

In KP, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat.

Additional input by Ameer Hamza and Tariq Naqash

World.title: Electoral rolls shrink by 589,458 in less than two months as ECP removes 1.48m deceased voters
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s electoral rolls contracted by 589,458 voters between May 7 and July 2, 2026, as the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) removed a large number of deceased voters from the electoral database, more than offsetting fresh registrations during the period, it emerged on Sunday.

According to official ECP statistics analysed by Dawn, the total number of registered voters fell from 137,163,857 on May 7 to 136,574,399 on July 2.

A senior ECP official said 895,000 new voters were enrolled during the period, but the deletion of around 1.48 million deceased voters resulted in a net decline of 589,458 voters nationwide.

The number of male voters dropped from 73,286,821 to 72,835,859, a decrease of 450,962, while female voters declined from 63,877,036 to 63,738,540, down by 138,496.

The reduction narrowed the gender gap among registered voters from about 941,000 to 910,000. Overall, 99 of the country’s 144 districts recorded a decline in registered voters, while 45 districts posted a net increase.

Punjab

Punjab accounted for the overwhelming share of the decline. The province lost 478,909 voters, with the total falling from 77,955,543 to 77,476,634, representing 81.2 per cent of the nationwide reduction.

Nine of the 10 districts with the largest declines were in Punjab.

According to ECP figures, Faisalabad recorded the largest decrease, with 41,264 voter entries removed, bringing the district’s total down from 56,18,044 to 55,76,780.

It was followed by Sheikhupura, with a decline of 31,783 voters, from 22,68,275 to 22,36,492; Gujranwala, with a drop of 30,302 voters, from 29,79,820 to 29,49,518; and Sialkot, which lost 30,129 voters, bringing the number down from 29,84,882 to 29,54,753.

The number of voters in Gujrat dropped by 29,553, followed by Sargodha with a decline of 26,675, Multan with 26,420, Kasur with 24,367 and Bahawalpur with 22,259.

Likewise, Khanewal saw a decline of 19,504 voters, Rahim Yar Khan 18,574, Lahore 16,633, Narowal 15,914, Toba Tek Singh 15,395, Rawalpindi 13,577, Mandi Bahauddin 13,480 and Attock 11,180.

The number of voters in Nankana Sahib and Muzaffargarh declined by over 10,000 each. Another nine districts saw a decrease of over 5,000 each. These included Okara, which saw a decline of 9,784 voters; Khushab, 8,226; Chakwal, 7,377; Dera Ghazi Khan, 6,755; Wazirabad, 6,723; Rajanpur, 6,621; Kot Addu, 6,358; Lodhran, 6,348; and Chiniot, 5,396.

Sindh

Sindh recorded the second-largest provincial decline, losing 97,216 voters, with the total dropping from 28,772,963 to 28,675,747.

Karachi South recorded the largest decline in the province, with 20,243 fewer voters, making it the only non-Punjab district among the top 10 districts with the biggest declines.

The number of voters in the district fell from 13,30,682 to 13,10,439. It was followed by Karachi East, where the removal of 16,873 voters brought the total down from 18,15,780 to 17,98,907. Keamari lost 9,983 voters, Karachi West 8,394, Hyderabad 7,573, Khairpur 7,228 and Sanghar 6,240.

KP

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) recorded a comparatively small net decline of 9,046 voters, with the provincial total falling from 23,415,995 to 23,406,949. However, it was the only province where more districts recorded gains than losses.

In overall terms, the province lost 9,049 voters, accounting for 1.53 per cent of the total decline. While the number of male voters slipped by 16,884, the number of female voters increased by 7,838.

Haripur lost 4,978 votes, followed by Abbottabad with 4,182, Charsadda with 3,946, Kohat with 3,352, Nowshera with 3,313, Lower Dir with 3,153 and DI Khan with 2,895.

Other districts to have lost over 2,000 votes included Mardan, Hangu and Bannu.

Balochistan

In Balochistan, the number of voters declined by 2,226, accounting for a 0.38pc decrease. The total fell from 57,65,008 to 57,62,782, reducing the number of male voters by 6,518 while increasing the number of female voters by 4,292.

Loralai and Sibi saw declines of 1,048 and 1,025, respectively. Most districts recorded marginal changes, restricted to two or three digits.

Islamabad Capital Territory saw a small decline of 2,061 voters, from 12,54,348 to 12,52,287. Those removed from the electoral rolls comprised 1,118 men and 940 women.

Despite the overall decline, 45 districts recorded an increase in registered voters between May 7 and July 2. KP led the gains, with 20 of its 36 districts adding voters. Of Balochistan’s 36 districts, 13 saw an increase, while nine of Sindh’s 30 districts recorded a rise in voter numbers. In Punjab, only three of the province’s 41 districts witnessed an increase in the voter count.

In KP, the biggest increase was recorded in Peshawar, which added 4,835 voters, taking the total from 22,46,457 to 22,51,292. Other major gains in the province included Bajaur with 3,797, Lower Dir with 3,153, Buner with 1,738 and Mansehra with 1,603. Other districts with increases of over 1,000 included Malakand, Khyber and South Waziristan (Lower).

In Balochistan, Quetta remained ahead with an increase of 4,052 voters, followed by Pishin, which saw an addition of 2,523 voters. In 11 other districts, the increase ranged between 65 and 573.

Sindh also saw growth in nine districts. Karachi Central recorded the highest increase in the province, with 4,428 new voters, rising from 22,60,158 to 22,64,586. Jacobabad gained 3,928 voters, Ghotki 2,479, Naushahro Feroze 2,103 and Korangi 1,024. Other districts with nominal growth included Larkana, Malir, Tharparkar and Thatta.

In Punjab, only three districts saw gains, which were offset by much larger deletions elsewhere. The largest increase was recorded in Bahawalnagar, where the number of voters surged by 16,094, from 20,12,083 in May to 20,28,177 in July, followed by Sahiwal with 4,755 and Vehari with 1,089.

World.title: Scuffle and chaos mar MQM-P meeting as two groups clash at party's Bahadurabad office
World.content:
KARACHI: At least four people were injured as a scuffle and chaos marred a meeting of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) at the party’s headquarters in Bahadurabad near Char Minar on Sunday evening.

According to party officials, the clash broke out between supporters of two rival groups within the party.

A police officer, requesting anonymity, told Dawn that police were present at the scene and the situation was under control. He added that, so far, no one had approached the New Town police to lodge a complaint.

The official added that police contingents had rushed to the scene to prevent the situation from deteriorating further.

Another police official told Dawn that at around 7:20pm, an MQM-P meeting was underway at the party’s temporary headquarters in Bahadurabad, where senior leaders were present.

He said the situation escalated after Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui left the meeting, with a scuffle breaking out between workers belonging to groups led by Anis Qaimkhani and Mustafa Kamal, and those supporting Dr Siddiqui and Aminul Haque.

According to the official, workers from the Qaimkhani group allegedly assaulted members of the Siddiqui group and forcibly removed them from the party’s headquarters. Later, Siddiqui group workers gathered at a nearby park.

The official said heavy firing was also reported from inside the party headquarters, causing fear and panic in the area.

One person, identified as Amir Ali, 40, sustained a bullet injury and was shifted to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital.

Later, Farooq Sattar, Ali Khursheedi and Haque arrived at the park and asked the workers to come for a press conference, which did not take place, the police officer added.

At around 10pm, the leaders left the party headquarters and the workers also dispersed.

Police remained present at the site, but no arrests were made, the official added.

Meanwhile, police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed said one person with a firearm injury and three others injured by sticks and stones were brought to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital from Bahadurabad.

She added that the person with the firearm injury, who had wounds on his arm and chest, was later shifted to a private hospital.

In a post on X, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said: “They set out to divide Sindh, but failed to keep their own house in order.”

“Those who sought to divide others have themselves splintered into factions today. The people have once again given a fitting response to those who pursued the politics of hatred against Sindh’s unity,” Javed said.

“Every dream of dividing Sindh was buried before, and it has been buried once again today. Sindh was united, Sindh is united and Sindh will remain united.”
